articles.title: More than the Score - Afcon: Is the Senegal v Morocco saga finally over? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstates Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions
articles.body:
World Service , · 28 Nov 2026 , · 23 mins

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions, 10 months after one of the most controversial games in football history - and eight months after the Confederation of African Football overturned the result of the final and awarded the trophy to Morocco instead. But is this really the end of the story? More than the Score's John Bennett is joined by Senegalese journalist Babacar Diarra and North African football expert Maher Mezahi to discuss the decision, and the impact of the saga on the game in Africa. We also hear from former Premier League referee Graham Scott, who gives his take on the decisions that were made, as well as former Nigeria striker Daniel Amokachi. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Plus, we've got the expertise of the BBC's top journalists, who share their insights from decades of covering sport at all levels. articles.title: Marco Garcés: “Estamos en un momento difícil, pero confío mucho en la segunda vuelta”
articles.standfirst: El director de fútbol del Celta apuesta por revertir la dinámica y maneja varias operaciones para reforzar la plantilla en enero si es necesario
articles.summary: El director de fútbol del Celta apuesta por revertir la dinámica y maneja varias operaciones para reforzar la plantilla en enero si es necesario
articles.body: El director de fútbol del Celta, Marco Garcés (1972, Ciudad de México), atiende a MARCA. Teme un final de año complicado, pero confía en su equipo y en Claudio Giráldez. No descarta fichajes en enero ni las salidas de Bayindir y Faye. Pregunta. ¿Qué balance hace del primer tercio de temporada? Respuesta. Ha sido difícil, duro, en el que hemos ido de menos a más. Las últimas fechas nos dan para ilusionarnos, pensando que vamos por buen rumbo. Sin embargo, la cosecha de puntos ha sido baja, tanto en Europa League como en LaLiga. P. Ahora llega con un final de año muy exigente, en cuanto a partidos R. Estamos en un momento muy difícil del equipo y creo que la cosa se va a poner más difícil antes de mejorar, pero confío mucho en que hagamos una segunda vuelta muy importante que nos permita alcanzar los objetivos que estamos buscando. Confío mucho en Claudio, en su cuerpo técnico y en la plantilla que tenemos, que es prácticamente la misma que consiguió grandes logros. P. Por lo tanto, ¿no descarta que el equipo pueda llegar a final de 2026 en una situación delicada? R. El rol de partidos que nos queda es muy exigente y creo que las cosas se van a poner difíciles, pero ratifico la confianza plena que tengo en que haremos una segunda vuelta importante. P. En Europa League las apreturas son mayores, ¿confía en el equipo en este torneo? R. Este es un equipo que, cuando las fichas están puestas, te puede dar más. En este tipo de partidos damos un esfuerzo extra y podemos sacar puntos. Confío en que podamos sacar los resultados para pasar de ronda. P. En Europa también está en juego lo económico; no pasar la fase de grupos posiblemente obligaría a realizar ventas en verano... R. Exactamente. El dinero que te permite la Europa League e ir progresando en rondas da más tranquilidad en el tema financiero. P. ¿Qué problema ha detectado en el arranque de temporada? R. No hemos producido la cantidad de oportunidades de gol a las que estábamos acostumbrados. Ha cambiado el modelo de juego. P. ¿Borja Iglesias ha sido una baja importante? R. Es una pieza fundamental de la planificación del club y del equipo, de la misma manera que Starfelt y Miguel Román, que han sido bajas importantes. Son piezas fundamentales dentro de la columna vertebral, piezas sobre las que armas la plantilla. Todo ello sin menospreciar el paso que han dado al frente Burcio, Antañón o Yoel Lago. P. ¿Esperaba más de los fichajes? R. Sebastián Cáceres me parece muy positivo, ha tenido muy buen arranque y es alguien en el que podemos confiar. Con Driouech necesitamos tiempo y Faye y Bayindir han tenido muy pocas oportunidades. P. Bayindir y Faye están cedidos, pero ¿pueden salir en enero? R. Será una conversación a mantener con sus clubes de origen porque ambos tienen algunas opciones distintas. Nos tendremos que sentar y contemplar las distintas variables. P. Si saliesen en enero, ¿cubrirían esas plazas? R. Nos obligaría a realizar algún movimiento. P. ¿Y alguno a mayores? R. Con Claudio barajamos varias opciones. Nuestra obligación es siempre tener opciones. Claudio tiene muy claro lo que necesita y veremos. Queda un mes y habrá que ver cómo llegan los lesionados. P. ¿Se apostará este año más por la Copa? R. Claudio es una bestia competitiva. Siempre va a por todas y quiere que el equipo tenga protagonismo en todo. P. Iago Aspas se retira y la próxima temporada estará en la secretaría técnica. ¿Saben ya su función? R. Iago es un tipo fenomenal, que es una alegría trabajar con él. Va a ser muy fácil encontrar una manera de trabajar juntos. Conoce a todos los futbolistas del mundo y será cuestión de que vaya encontrando su ruta y vocación. P. El club vive una época dorada con el primer equipo en Europa y el filial debutando en Segunda… R. Lo vivimos con una gran carga de trabajo porque parece que jugamos todos los días pero quiero creer que esto son buenas noticias. Tener al Celta Fortuna en Segunda para nosotros es un orgullo. Hay muchos jugadores de ese equipo que tienen una pinta bárbara, que pueden ser jugadores importantes de Primera. P. ¿Salvará la categoría el Celta Fortuna? R. Me está encantando su temporada. Hemos tenido errores gruesos que prácticamente todos nos han castigado pero confío en que haremos una segunda vuelta mejor que la primera y hasta el momento no hemos tocado el descenso.

articles.title: Atlético - Viking | Que se enteren los vikingos...
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos solo contemplan un triunfo ante el equipo noruego
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos solo contemplan un triunfo ante el equipo noruego
articles.body: “Jugadores, jugadores, hemos venido a ganar, que se enteren los vikingos quién manda en la capital”. Aunque no se trate de un derbi, el cántico tantas veces entonado por la afición del Atlético en la antesala de medirse a su eterno rival bien sirve como advertencia al Viking en la primera visita de su historia al Metropolitano: los rojiblancos no pueden permitirse más tropiezos que compliquen la posición que se han ganado en el continente desde que Simeone se hiciera cargo del banquillo conquistando la Copa, primero, y convirtiera a su equipo en un fijo de las rondas de eliminación de la Champions, en las temporadas sucesivas. Del mismo modo que caer en Anfield en el estreno de este curso en la única competición que se resiste al Cholo y ceder los tres puntos en el paso como un rodillo del todopoderoso Bayern Munich por Madrid podrían entrar en el guion, la victoria frente al modesto campeón de la última Liga de Noruega (en la actual perdió el liderato en favor del Bodo Glimt tras la derrota del pasado fin de semana) también se antoja innegociable. No ya por la falta de peso del Viking en el panorama continental (lo compensa con la ilusión y la valentía con la que consiguió sorprender al Bayern y arañarle una igualada), sino por los cuatro puntos en el casillero (resultado de vencer al Manchester United y empatar en Stuttgart) que obligan al Atlético a escalar puestos en la tabla. En este sentido, conducidos por el partido a partido en cualquier competición, la máxima de Simeone cobra más relevancia que nunca con el nuevo sistema de la liguilla. Por eso, lo primero es sumar los tres puntos frente al Viking que le consoliden entre los 24 clubes que sigan adelante. Luego ya vendrán las visitas al PSV y al Bodo y el partido frente al Fenerbahce en casa que determinen si los puntos alcanzan para colarse en el top 8 que evite una ronda más antes de plantarse en los octavos. Una clasificación, en todo caso, que la propia experiencia rojiblanca evidencia que nunca se sabe cuál es el camino más despejado hacia la ansiada final en el Metropolitano: hace dos campañas, tras acabar entre los ocho mejores, el Atlético se toparía en octavos con el Real Madrid (eliminación con el doble toque de Julián Alvarez mediante), mientras que la pasada, tras tener que disputar el playoff frente al Brujas, los de Simeone acabarían asomándose hasta las semifinales frente al Arsenal. También el pasado más reciente sirve al Atlético para recordar el coste de un despiste en la Champions, pues si tuvo que jugarse la continuidad en la anterior edición frente al Brujas, fue precisamente por doblar la rodilla ante su afición frente a un conjunto noruego, un Bodo Glimt en este caso que se confirmó como la gran sorpresa. De ahí que no haya lugar para las confianzas, sino para dar continuidad a la fiabilidad del Atlético en el presente ejercicio (manifestada en su máxima expresión con el mejor inicio de su historia en las salidas a domicilio) y a la fortaleza que viene mostrando desde que se levantó el Metropolitano. De hecho, de los 61 visitantes que precedieron al estreno del Viking, 26 perdieron siempre, mientras que la nómina de los que no han logrado llevarse el triunfo asciende hasta 45, el 74% de los equipos que se han presentado en el feudo rojiblanco. Así las cosas, el Atlético tiene muy claro su objetivo para esta noche, ahora sólo falta que también se enteren los vikingos de lo que les espera.

articles.title: Pitchwise Holdings no estará en la Junta General del Valencia
articles.standfirst: Fuentes cercanas al nuevo accionista del club de Mestalla aseguran que Corey Woolfolk y Ann Rodríguez esperarán antes de desembarcar en Valencia
articles.summary: Fuentes cercanas al nuevo accionista del club de Mestalla aseguran que Corey Woolfolk y Ann Rodríguez esperarán antes de desembarcar en Valencia
articles.body: El Valencia presentará sus cuentas el próximo 9 de diciembre. En esa fecha está fijada una de las Juntas Generales Ordinarias del club de Mestalla más importantes de su historia. El movimiento accionarial, aprobado ya por el CSD y a expensas de un trámite burocrático para hacerse oficial, en el que Peter Lim ha vendido el 42% de la sociedad anónima deportiva a un fondo de inversión americano, ha sacudido el mapa de poder del club. Pitchwise Holdings ha entrado de lleno en el control de la entidad y las nuevas cabezas visibles del club, al margen de su presidente y máximo accionista Kiat Lim, hijo del empresario de Singapur, son Ann Rodríguez y Carey Woolfolf. Sin embargo, según ha podido confirmar MARCA con fuentes cercanas al fondo de inversión americano, ninguno de ellos estará presente en la Junta General Ordinaria que presidirá Kiat Lim. De momento se va a esperar para hacer oficial el desembarco e ir tomando posiciones dentro del consejo de administración al que aún no pertenecen. La idea es que Corey y Ann no estén en Valencia, pero aún faltan un par de semanas para la Junta, nuevamente abierta a los accionistas tras la época de oscurantismo. Hay que recordar que el fondo americano ya ha empezado a trabajar para el club aunque falte un papel para dar rienda suelta a la operación. De hecho, Corey estuvo reunido más de seis horas con Javier Solis, director general de la entidad y Braulio Vázquez, director deportivo, en Madrid para trazar las líneas del mercado de enero y dar algunas pinceladas de sus intenciones deportivas.

articles.title: Arribas se sienta en el trono del gol rojiblanco
articles.standfirst: El madrileño alcanza los 50 goles y se convierte en el máximo goleador rojiblanco de la historia del club en el fútbol profesional
articles.summary: El madrileño alcanza los 50 goles y se convierte en el máximo goleador rojiblanco de la historia del club en el fútbol profesional
articles.body: Sergio Arribas sigue acumulando motivos para ser considerado uno de los futbolistas más importantes de la historia reciente de la UD Almería. El atacante madrileño firmó un doblete en la noche de ayer en Ceuta, en un partido que pasará a la historia por permitirle alcanzar los 50 goles con la camiseta rojiblanca. Una cifra que le convierte en el máximo goleador del club en el fútbol profesional, superando todos los registros logrados por jugadores del conjunto indálico entre Primera y Segunda División. Aunque el ranking absoluto de goleadores continúa encabezado por Ortiz Bernal (59) y Raúl Sánchez (57), ambos construyeron buena parte de esos registros en categorías no profesionales. Arribas, por el contrario, ha firmado sus 50 tantos exclusivamente en el fútbol profesional: 18 en Primera y 32 en Segunda. Un mérito que le sitúa en la cima de una clasificación que refleja el rendimiento de los jugadores del Almería en la élite. El medio centenar de goles tampoco es una cifra cualquiera dentro de la historia rojiblanca. Antes del madrileño solo Raúl Sánchez y Ortiz Bernal habían conseguido alcanzar esa barrera. El primero lo logró en la temporada 2001/02 y el segundo repitió la hazaña en la campaña 2006/07. Casi dos décadas después, Arribas se suma a ese reducido grupo y lo hace, además, convirtiéndose en el primer futbolista que alcanza ese registro íntegramente en el fútbol profesional. Existe, además, una llamativa coincidencia entre las tres efemérides. Raúl, Ortiz Bernal y ahora Arribas alcanzaron los 50 goles gracias a un doblete. Una casualidad que cobra todavía más relevancia al recordar que en las dos ocasiones anteriores el Almería terminó celebrando un ascenso: a Segunda División en 2002 y a Primera en 2007. Un precedente que invita al optimismo en una temporada en la que el conjunto dirigido por García Pimienta vuelve a luchar por regresar a la máxima categoría. Más allá del simbolismo del récord, el registro de Arribas es el premio a una trayectoria marcada por la constancia. Desde su llegada procedente del Real Madrid Castilla, el atacante ha ido incrementando su peso específico en el equipo hasta convertirse en la gran referencia ofensiva del proyecto. Tras firmar dos campañas de adaptación en Primera División y explotar definitivamente el pasado curso con el Pichichi de Segunda, el madrileño ha seguido elevando sus prestaciones para entrar definitivamente en la historia del club. Con apenas 25 años, Arribas ya puede presumir de ser el futbolista que más goles ha marcado con la UD Almería en el fútbol profesional. Un récord que refuerza su condición de icono del almeriensismo y que, visto su rendimiento y su protagonismo, todavía tiene margen para seguir creciendo.

articles.title: Iraizoz y el gol que anuló Mateu
articles.standfirst: El portero del Athletic marcó ante el Málaga en agosto de 2014, pero el árbitro atendió la reclamación de su asistente, que consideró había fuera de juego posicional de Laporte
articles.summary: El portero del Athletic marcó de cabeza ante el Málaga en agosto de 2014, pero el árbitro atendió la reclamación de su asistente al levantar el banderín por un fuera de juego posicional
articles.body: El Athletic regresa este sábado a La Rosaleda, escenario que no pisa desde el curso 17-18 y en el que sólo ha ganado uno de sus últimos cinco partidos (4 de Liga y 1 de Copa). El campo de Paseo de Martiricos fue escenario de una jugada más que desagradable para Iraizoz. En agosto de 2014 el portero marcó de cabeza en el descuento de un partido que el Athletic iba perdiendo por 1-0, pero el tanto fue invalidado por fuera de juego posicional de Laporte. “No nos quedó muy claro porque el árbitro decía una cosa y el linier otra”, explicó entonces Iraizoz. El navarro habría pasado a la historia por ser el primer portero del Athletic en marcar durante un partido oficial, pero en un fútbol sin VAR ni fuera de juego automático o semiautomático mandó la percepción del asistente. Y éste entendió que antes de la falta lanzada por Ibai el central Laporte estba en fuera de juego posicional, alterando la posibilidad de despeje del futbolista más cercano a Iraizoz. El equipo que entrenaba Valverde no acusó la derrota de Málaga y días después salió adelante en la eliminatoria de acceso a Champions frente al Nápoles que se disputó en San Mamés. El portero pidió explicaciones a Mateu cuando coincidieron, ya duchados, a la salida de vestuarios. Eso sí, Iraizoz cuidó mucho sus formas y no quiso un escándalo con la anulación. “Da mucha rabia cuando ayudamos al equipo a sacar las cosas adelante y haces méritos para conseguir los puntos. Mateu se ha equivocado, ha sido un gol claro y lo han anulado. Somos humanos y lo comprendo porque soy portero y se lo que significan los fallos”, expresó. El recuerdo al remate de Iraizoz sigue presente entre los aficionados del Athletic. Y la frescura se aviva porque el pasado viernes, en el encuentro que los leones jugaron en San Mamés ante el Espanyol, Simón fue a rematar una acción de balón parado con el tiempo cumplido cuando el conjunto perico ganaba por 0-1. El internacional rojiblanco, a diferencia de Iraizoz, no tuvo opción de conectar con el balón.

articles.title: Del Nido Benavente introduce un complemento para limitar el sueldo a los consejeros del Sevilla
articles.standfirst: El ex presidente se alía con el sevillismo de base a menos de dos semanas de la Junta
articles.summary: El ex presidente se alía con el sevillismo de base a menos de dos semanas de la Junta
articles.body: A algo más de 15 días de la celebración de la Junta General de Accionistas del Sevilla, la Federación de Peñas, junto a Accionistas Unidos y José María del Nido Benavente, han trasladado con éxito al Sevilla Fútbol Club un escrito mediante el cual solicita incluir un punto en la Junta del próximo 10 de diciembre donde se trate la revisión de los sueldos del consejo. El sevillismo de base, de la mano del ex presidente, reclaman reducir el salario de los miembros del consejo de administración, especialmente del presidente José María del Nido Carrasco y los miembros del comité ejecutivo. Una petición que cumple los requisitos que marca la ley de sociedades de capital por tener más de un 5% del capital social y tendrá que aparecer como punto -será el 8- en el orden del día. Del Nido Benavente pide modificar el artículo 30 de los estatutos de la sociedad, relacionado con la retribución de los administradores, que considera "verdaderamente inconcebible" ante "las cuantiosas pérdidas que recurrentemente se vienen generando año tras año". Por eso solicita que los salarios dependan de que la sociedad genere beneficios, en concreto "consistirá en un porcentaje del 5% de los beneficios líquidos o repartibles del ejercicio". Además, correspondería a la Junta General de Accionistas "determinar el importe exacto a distribuir entre los miembros del órgano de administración dentro del limite estatutario antes fijado, así como los criterios de asignación". Si el ejercicio arroja pérdidas o el patrimonio neto de la entidad resulta negativo, "no se devengará retribución alguna". Eso sí, "a los consejeros se les abonarán o reembolsarán los gastos razonables y debidamente justificados en que hubiesen incurrido como consecuencia de su asistencia a reuniones y seis tareas directamente relacionadas con el desempeño de su cargo, tales como desplazamiento, alojamiento, manutención y gastos de representación".

articles.title: Edward Iordanescu: Watford appoint Romanian as new head coach
articles.summary: Watford appoint former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu as their new head coach after sacking Alessio Dionisi.
articles.body:
Watford have appointed former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu as the Championship club's new head coach.

The 48-year-old replaces Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge following a run of seven defeats in their past 10 league games, culminating in Saturday's 4-0 loss to Sheffield United.

"I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," Iordanescu told the club website. , external

"I can see the team is in a difficult moment but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days and I'm very confident about the future."

He becomes Watford's sixth new boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford

The former CFR Cluj and Legia Warsaw manager will be joined at Watford by backroom staff Alexandru Radu, Grzegorz Mokry and Michele Iannucci, but will watch Wednesday's Championship match at home to Blackburn Rovers from the stands before taking charge for Saturday's game at Derby.

Adrian Mariappa will oversee Wednesday's match at Vicarage Road (19:45 GMT), alongside Paul Furlong and Lloyd Doyley.

The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, where he won the Super Cup last season.

It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season.

He also spent two-and-a-half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands.

Iordanescu takes over a Watford side currently three points above the relegation zone , having won only four of their 16 games so far.

Who is Iordanescu and what is he facing?

Although untried in English football, Watford are getting a trophy-winning head coach with a wide-ranging CV spanning spells in his homeland, Bulgaria and Poland, as well as elite-level international experience with Romania.

His connections with his national side run deep as the son of his country's legendary former head coach Anghel Iordanescu, who famously took them to the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup during a reign of more than 100 games.

It is likely he will need every bit of that nous and inspiration as he becomes the latest boss to try to revive a club which continues to plough through managers at an alarming rate.

Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, with Iordanescu becoming the sixth permanent boss since Tom Cleverley was sacked in May 2025.

The Hornets' slow start to the season - with only four home wins and one point out of 24 away - has played out against the backdrop of uncertainty and unrest off the pitch.

Watford's owner, Gino Pozzo, is currently standing trial in Spain as one of a number of defendants accused of tax offences relating to Spanish team Granada, a club he used to be associated with.

He denies the allegations, which are related to player trading at Granada.

The case continues a tumultuous period for the club, with supporter and former owner Elton John voicing his frustration after a 4-0 home defeat by Burnley last month.

Fans have also questioned the running of the club, with one supporters' group declaring a loss of confidence in the ownership.

Iordanescu's immediate concern will be improving results, particularly Watford's form on the road, where they have yet to win and have conceded 18 goals in eight matches - with only Burnley letting in more.

He arrives with a reputation for defensive organisation and stability, of which the Hornets are in desperate need.

Iordanescu 'thrown in at deep end' - analysis

Geoff Doyle, BBC Three Counties Radio sports editor

So Watford try again with a new head coach - it is a regular occurrence at Vicarage Road.

Iordanescu has a decent CV with his work overseas in Romania, Bulgaria and Poland and is well thought of as a coach and manager.

But a lack of Championship experience is a concern and he is thrown in at the deep end with his new team hovering just above the relegation zone and confidence and morale low.

Iordanescu needs to hit the ground running in a critical week with the Hornets up against mid-table Blackburn and then Derby who are in the relegation zone.

articles.title: 'Mourinhinas' y remontadas para el Real Madrid de Champions
articles.standfirst: Tres de las cinco victorias han llegado dándole la vuelta al marcador
articles.summary: Tres de las cinco victorias han llegado dándole la vuelta al marcador
articles.body: En 1988, el Real Madrid, que venía de eliminar sucesivamente (en la Copa de Europa no había liguillas, ni tradicionales ni suizas) al Nápoles (de Maradona), al Oporto (defensor del título) y al Bayern de Múnich (verdugo de los blancos en el curso anterior y, entonces sí, bestia negra del Madrid). Esa parecía por fin la Copa de Europa del Madrid, que llevaba sin olerla desde 1966. Pero aquel equipo, el de la gloriosa Quinta del Buitre, quizá infravaloró a los holandeses, que por otra parte tenían un equipazo. Y toneladas de suerte. De hecho, ganaron el torneo después de empatar cinco partidos seguidos, incluida la final ante el Benfica. Algo parecido pudo pasar anoche. El PSV llegaba a Madrid con apenas cuatro puntos, muy lejos del deslumbrante registro de los blancos, cuatro victorias en otros tantos partidos. No parecía una tarea complicada, pero hubo que aplicar una fórmula que el Madrid ha tenido que explotar de forma recurrente en esta edición de la Champions, la de la remontada. Como ante Roma y AEK de Atenas, el Madrid tuvo que verse por detrás en el marcador para desplegar su mejor juego. No es una frase hecha. Seguramente el equipo realizó anoche los mejores 45 minutos de la temporada. Hasta el punto de que el PSV, que se había enseñoreado del Bernabéu en el primer acto, se diluyó como un azucarillo. La entrada en el terreno de juego de Bellingham, sobre todo, pero también de dos nuevos centrales (Konaté y Huijsen) en lugar de la pareja titular (Militao y Rüdiger) cambió radicalmente el partido. El Madrid, dominado antes del pausa, fue un vendaval liderado por Bellingham, el jugador más en forma del equipo, por mucho que Mbappé sea, de largo, el más productivo de cara al arco rival. El cambio llegó desde el banquillo. Como en Roma, cuando Mou apostó por un doble pivote Fede-Tchouaméni con el que los giallorossi lograron una renta de dos goles. La salida al campo de Güler y Bernardo, y luego las de Endrick y Espí, permitió al Madrid una remontada vibrante, sellada en la recta final de un duelo que dejó mudo al Olímpico. En Atenas la intervención de Mou no fue tan decisiva. De nuevo el Madrid salió con la caraja y los griegos se adelantaron muy pronto. Reaccionaron los blancos, pero en una jugada aislada los locales volvieron a ponerse por delante. Empató de nuevo el Madrid a falta de unos diez minutos... y a partir de ahí, el asedio, coronado en esta ocasión por un tremendo derechazo de Fede Valverde,, que volvió a ser protagonista ayer ante el PSV, con el gol que abría el camino a la remontada. En todas las remontadas hay un denominador común: Jose Mourinho. El entrenador portugués está interviniendo con éxito, tanto con los cambios como con su discurso. Las 'mourinhinas' por ahora funcionan, porque en el descanso ante el PSV hubo más que palabras. Con mano izquierda, pero el discurso de Mou fue clave. Lo admitieron hasta los jugadores. Los blancos, en suma, atesoran ya 15 puntos en cinco partidos de la Fase Liga, todos los posibles, que les sitúan en una posición de privilegio para lograr algo que estuvo fuera de su alcance en las dos últimas temporadas: evitar el playoff.

articles.title: Henry avisa a Europa: "Algo está pasando en el Real Madrid, cuidado"
articles.standfirst: El exjugador francés alertó en su análisis lo que está mejorando el equipo blanco
articles.summary: El exjugador francés alertó en su análisis lo que está mejorando el equipo blanco
articles.body: una de las voces más autorizadas del fútbol europeo, Thierry Henry, lanzó un mensaje que sonó a advertencia para todos los aspirantes a la Champions: "Algo está pasando en el Madrid, cuidado". La contundente victoria blanca en casa ante el PSV dejó claro que el Real Madrid ha adquirido una suerte de velocidad de crucero que, cuando menos, supone un aviso a navegantes a estas alturas del campeonato. El exdelantero francés analizó en CBS Sports el momento que atraviesa el equipo de José Mourinho y llegó a una conclusión clara: el conjunto blanco está creciendo a gran velocidad. "El Madrid ha hecho un gran partido. Jugando así es candidato a la Champions. Está creciendo mucho con el paso de las semanas", afirmó. Las palabras de Henry no se limitan al resultado ante el PSV. El francés pone el foco en una tendencia. El Madrid encadena 10 victorias consecutivas (cinco en liga y cinco en Champions) y está mostrando una capacidad de reacción que recuerda a sus mejores noches europeas. Ante el conjunto neerlandés volvió a quedar patente: pasó del 0-1 al descanso a un incontestable 5-1 final. Uno de los factores que más ha llamado la atención al exinternacional galo es el nivel de Jude Bellingham. El inglés volvió a liderar al equipo y recibió un elogio rotundo de Henry. "Bellingham es increíble. Llevar el '5' en el Madrid no es fácil, pero él hace que parezca sencillo. Su personalidad es increíble", destacó sobre un futbolista que vuelve a marcar diferencias en los grandes escenarios. Henry también quiso reivindicar la figura de Vinicius Junior, otro de los nombres propios de la noche. "Hace unos meses estaban matando a Vinicius y miradle ahora", señaló el francés, convencido de que el brasileño ha recuperado la versión que le convirtió en uno de los jugadores más decisivos del continente. Más allá de los elogios individuales, el análisis de Henry refleja una sensación cada vez más extendida en Europa: este Madrid empieza a transmitir algo distinto. Hay resultados, pero también una identidad cada vez más reconocible, una conexión creciente entre sus estrellas y una competitividad que lleva el sello de Mourinho.

articles.title: Ex-England star Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling admitted inhaling ‘laughing ⁠gas’ and driving erratically before crashing his car.
articles.body:
Former England winger Raheem Sterling has been ⁠spared ⁠an immediate jail sentence after he admitted dangerous driving by inhaling “laughing ⁠gas” while behind the wheel before crashing his Lamborghini.

Sterling, 31, was reported ⁠driving erratically on the M25 and M3 motorways in southern England during the morning rush hour on May 28, with witnesses saying ‌he was inhaling from a balloon and weaving between lanes.

Police later found Sterling sitting in the passenger seat of his crashed car holding two canisters of nitrous oxide. No other vehicles were ⁠involved and no injuries were ⁠reported.

Sterling, who most recently played for Dutch side Feyenoord, pleaded guilty in September to dangerous driving, possession ⁠of nitrous oxide and failing to provide a blood specimen.

He ⁠appeared for sentencing on Wednesday at ⁠Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court, where Judge Kirsty Allman said Sterling had acted with “conscious disregard for the safety of other ‌road users”.

But, she added, Sterling had substantial personal mitigation, including his charitable work and his engagement with addiction services since the incident.

She sentenced Sterling to 12 months’ imprisonment, suspended for 18 months, and ‌ordered ‌him to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.

Sterling won 82 England caps, the last of which came at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The winger, currently without a club, made his senior debut at Liverpool before joining City in 2015, winning four Premier League titles.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but subsequently fell out of favour and spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Feyenoord on a short-term deal in February, playing eight times in the Eredivisie, but left at the end of the season.

articles.title: Hours after reported Ben Shelton breakup, Trinity Rodman pulls out of USA’s CONCACAF W Championship roster
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman pulls out of the USA's CONCACAF W Championship roster after suffering a shoulder injury, coinciding with the news of her breakup with tennis star Ben Shelton.
articles.body: Trinity Rodman was preparing for another international assignment after a demanding NWSL season, but her plans took an unexpected turn just hours after reports emerged that she and tennis star Ben Shelton had called time on their relationship. The Washington Spirit forward now faces another development that has put her upcoming USWNT campaign in doubt.Rodman ruled out of CONCACAF W ChampionshipTrinity Rodman has withdrawn from the United States squad for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship, taking place in Texas from November 27 to December 5, 2026, after sustaining what US Soccer described as a minor shoulder injury.The federation announced that the 24-year-old would not be part of the 23-player squad for the tournament window in Texas. Head coach Emma Hayes has called up Gotham FC forward Jaedyn Shaw, who was born in Frisco, Texas, to replace her.Rodman injured her shoulder in the fifth minute of the NWSL Championship final on Saturday, November 21, following an aerial collision with Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse. She continued playing despite the problem and eventually scored a stoppage-time goal for the Washington Spirit, who lost the final 2-1.The forward's decision to withdraw allows her to recover from the injury rather than risk aggravating it during international duty. Her removal comes after an eventful weekend in which she played through the shoulder problem, scored in the championship defeat and was subsequently ruled out of the national team's plans.Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman reportedly end relationshipRodman's withdrawal was announced hours after the Daily Mail reported that she and Shelton had separated, ending a relationship that became public in March 2025.The pair had become one of American sport's most recognisable young couples, regularly appearing at each other's matches and making efforts to spend time together despite demanding schedules. However, according to the newspaper, their professional commitments and constant travel eventually made the relationship difficult to maintain.The outlet also reported that the couple remain close despite the split.Their schedules had often required them to travel considerable distances to support one another. Shelton, 24, spends much of the year competing on the ATP Tour, while Rodman's commitments with the Washington Spirit and the US women's national team have kept her travelling across the United States and internationally.The timing of their reported separation was notable: Shelton lost his ATP Finals semi-final to Carlos Alcaraz in Turin on Saturday, while Rodman and the Spirit were beaten in the NWSL Championship on the same evening.Shelton was subsequently seen at Madison Square Garden on Sunday for the New York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers. He attended without Rodman, sitting alongside actress Inde Navarette.From courtside support to the demands of two sporting careersRodman and Shelton first attracted attention as a couple in March 2025, initially hinting at their relationship through a TikTok trend before making it public.Their support for each other's careers was visible throughout the following months. Rodman became a regular presence in Shelton's player box during the US Open in September and had also travelled to support him at other tournaments, including Wimbledon in May 2025.On one occasion, she made a particularly demanding journey to watch him compete. After playing an NWSL match in Washington on the day of one of Shelton's US Open appearances, Rodman left the capital almost immediately after the final whistle to reach New York. She was later seen in tears at Arthur Ashe Stadium following Shelton's defeat by Alexander Zverev.Shelton also made time to support Rodman, including after the Washington Spirit's NWSL Championship defeat, when footage showed him consoling her as she cried on the sidelines.In September, Shelton spoke openly about the difficulties of maintaining a relationship while both athletes were pursuing demanding professional careers. Speaking to Us Weekly, he said:“It is really difficult. I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.”He continued:“Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.“This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Raheem Sterling - from national icon to suspended jail sentence
articles.summary: Fourteen years after making his Premier League debut at 17, Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended prison sentence.
articles.body:
Raheem Sterling grew up a stone's throw from Wembley Stadium, and went on to start a European Championship final for England there.

At his peak, the four-time Premier League winner was earning £325,000 a week at Chelsea .

"Raheem is a huge player with a huge influence in the last few years in English football," said then Blues boss Thomas Tuchel when he signed a 27-year-old Sterling in a £50m deal in 2022.

"He is at the perfect age to take responsibility around the younger players that we have and be an example.

"He just needs to do what he did over the last few years and he will be a huge asset for us."

Sterling enjoyed a 10-year England career, also played for Liverpool , Manchester City and Arsenal , and commanded combined transfer fees of about £100m.

But his career at the top level looks to be in the balance at the age of 31 after he was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving. Sterling has also been disqualified from driving for two years and ordered to carry out 100 hours of unpaid work.

At an earlier hearing in September, Sterling admitted dangerous driving on a motorway before crashing a Lamborghini on 28 May.

The crash caused "substantial" damage to his car and all four wheels, which prevented him from driving further, the court heard.

Sterling also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.

Sterling's life was touched by tragedy at a young age.

Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he was just two when his father was shot dead.

His mother, Nadine, was determined to give her children a safer environment to live in. She moved to England to lay a path for Sterling and his sister to join her once she had found a home and finished her education, while cleaning bathrooms and changing bedsheets in hotels to earn extra money.

Sterling grew up on a housing estate in Neasden, north-west London, and spent part of his education at Vernon House, where teachers attempted to help the football-obsessed youngster with behavioural problems.

In an interview with the Players' Tribune , external in 2018, Sterling said: "I was so naughty that they kicked me out of primary school. I just didn't like to listen to anyone but my mum. That was my problem."

He was 10 when teacher Chris Beschi told him: "If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or in prison."

Sterling would grow to become one of the standout English attacking talents of his generation.

Raheem Sterling: From school struggles to a class of his own

On 14 November 2012 - aged 17 years and 342 days - Sterling made his England debut on the night his Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard won his 100th cap in a 4-2 defeat by Sweden in Stockholm.

Sterling would go on to make 81 more appearances for his country, scoring 20 goals.

He featured at three World Cups - 2014, 2018 and 2022 - and two European Championships. He was one of the standout players as England reached the Euro 2020 final at Wembley, where they were beaten by Italy.

Sterling was now at the peak of his career - the former Queens Park Rangers youngster, who has a tattoo on his forearm of a young boy holding a football looking up at the Wembley arch, named in the team of the tournament by Uefa.

Liverpool had signed a 15-year-old Sterling from QPR for £600,000 in February 2010.

He made his senior Reds debut two years later and became the second-youngest goalscorer in their history - behind Michael Owen - when he scored the winner against Reading in October 2012 at the age of 17.

In 2015, Sterling joined Manchester City in a deal worth up to £49m, making him the most expensive English player at the time.

He had been under contract at Anfield until 2017 but turned down a new deal to move to Liverpool 's rivals, with City boss Manuel Pellegrini describing the 20-year-old as "one of the best attacking players in world football".

Sterling went on to score 131 goals in 339 appearances in all competitions during seven successful years at Etihad Stadium.

As well as four Premier League titles, he helped City win five League Cups, one FA Cup and one Community Shield.

It was while he was at City, in 2021, that Sterling became an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours for his services to racial equality in sport.

"I am grateful to have been recognised," he said. "But my priority is to try to help to educate society and myself. I'm learning every day."

After City came the move to Chelsea , where his career began to stall.

Tuchel, now England manager, was sacked two months after signing Sterling, who made just 45 Premier League starts for the Blues over four years.

Off the pitch, he launched a scholarship fund aimed at closing the gap in the number of black British students who go to university.

On the pitch, he was finding it a struggle.

He spent 18 months as a member of Chelsea 's so-called 'bomb squad' , and a season-long loan to Arsenal in 2024-25 proved largely unsuccessful.

'Sterling will look back and wonder' Published 17 April 2015

As well as his success on the field, Sterling has made headlines off it too.

In 2015, when he was 20, reports began to surface about his behaviour away from the game.

Sterling was pictured apparently inhaling nitrous oxide and was also photographed smoking a shisha pipe.

That prompted then Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers to warn Sterling he would "look back in 20 years and wonder what he was doing".

Sterling also made headlines while on duty for England at the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

The Sun ran a story titled "Raheem shoots himself in the foot" as pictures emerged of a tattoo of an M16 assault rifle on his leg.

Sterling explained on social media: "When I was 2 my father died from being gunned down to death I made a promise to myself I would never touch a gun in my life time. I shoot with my right foot so it has a deeper meaning."

The incident led to a widespread discussion in the UK about the treatment of black athletes in the media, with comparisons drawn between how Sterling's life was covered compared to others.

Sterling spoke out a number of times on the issue and wider racism in society, which was reflected in him being made an MBE.

Five years after his MBE, Sterling's career has stalled. He has not played since appearing for Feyenoord on 17 May, after agreeing a short-term move to the Netherlands.

Eleven days after that game, he was arrested after crashing a Lamborghini near the M3 in Hampshire.

Listen: From Wembley schoolboy to playing for England at Wembley

Sterling was riding the crest of a wave when he moved from Manchester City to Chelsea in the summer of 2022 for £50m.

His medal cabinet was already fit to burst with 10 major trophies under Guardiola and, alongside Harry Kane, he was arguably England's most important player for then head coach Gareth Southgate.

Tuchel viewed Sterling as his number one target that summer and Chelsea 's new ownership - Behdad Eghbali and Todd Boehly - delivered as the club entered the post-Roman Abramovich era.

Two months later, Tuchel was sacked and Graham Potter was in situ.

Sterling's career has not been the same since.

It is, of course, senseless to suggest the troubles Sterling has had on and off the pitch in recent years are simply down to the sacking of Tuchel in 2022.

But speak to those close to Sterling and they will explain Tuchel was among the key factors behind the winger's decision to swap Manchester for west London.

He was captivated by Tuchel's vision, not only for the team, but his role in it.

articles.title: Pep Guardiola Says He's Eying a National Team As Next Landing Spot, Talks Timeline Amid USMNT Rumors
articles.summary: Pep Guardiola has confirmed his next management job will be in international football amid ongoing rumors he could replace Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach of the United States men's national team.
articles.body:
Pep Guardiola has confirmed his next management job will be in international football amid ongoing rumors he could replace Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach of the United States men's national team.

Speaking with legendary Brazilian striker and his former teammate Romario, Pep noted his desire to take his first plunge into working with a major national team.

"A national team, which is my next step," he said, per Romario TV (h/t Pol Ballus & Ali Rampling of The Athletic).

Guardiola is reportedly U.S. Soccer's primary target to replace Pochettino, who cut short his tenure to join Manchester United last week, per The Athletic's Paul Tenorio, Henry Bushnell and Tom Bogert. He has already turned down the advances of Italy, a decision that didn't come lightly after the Italian FA placed its trust in him.

"I spoke with them," he said, per Romario TV . "It was an honour. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. It is one of the biggest honours I've had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop.

"If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it. But I told (Paulo) Maldini and Leonardo (Bonucci, FICG executives at the time), who I love so much, I needed to stop and spend a bit more time with myself. It's been 18 years of being there every day, every day."

Guardiola is also said to have established a verbal agreement to replace Gareth Southgate as England boss in 2024, per Jack Pitt-Brooke, Oliver Kay and David Ornstein of The Athletic. However, he remained in charge at Manchester City and the Three Lions opted for Thomas Tuchel instead.

Guardiola is arguably the greatest manager of his generation, having won an astonishing 41 trophies across his time with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Man City, including two continental trebles.

He confirmed his departure from the Etihad Stadium in May after a decade in which his side dominated the Premier League.

Man City has since been found guilty of serious financial breaches dating from 2009-2018, including inflating its income to the tune of approximately $1.19 billion. Guardiola released a statement of support while the club awaits its punishment.

Pep admits he is unsure of how much time he needs off before returning, and that he's in zero rush after an almost endless schedule since he retired as a player twenty years ago.

"I don't know how much time, though," he said, per Romario TV . "The truth is I don't know. Now I feel very well. I believe that if I ever return to football, it will be when my stomach tells me I need to be back, and someone wants me. Then we'll be back. But if not, I'm calm. It's been a lot of years and games."

Whichever nation scoops him up will receive an innovative coach, best known for the development of tiki-taka football and the rise of Lionel Messi during his iconic Barcelona career.

Guardiola is also an extremely intense individual who uses strict methods to build his teams. How that translates to international football, where he will receive limited time with his players, will be truly fascinating.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso descubre los abucheos de Stamford Bridge: "Entiendo su decepción y la compartimos"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Chelsea empatizó con la afición 'blue' tras la derrota ante el Leeds (1-4)
articles.summary: El entrenador del Chelsea empatizó con la afición 'blue' tras la derrota ante el Leeds (1-4)
articles.body: La paciencia es un bien que escasea en el Chelsea. Escaseaba con Roman Abramovich y escasea, más si cabe, desde la llegada de BlueCo. en 2022. Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Bruno Saltor, Frank Lampard, Mauricio Pochettino, Enzo Maresca y Calum McFarlane pueden dar fe de ello. Xabi Alonso ya conoce también de primera mano la impaciencia que sobrevuela Stamford Bridge. La goleada encajada ante el Leeds (1-4) provocó que la grada despidiera a los 'blues' entre silbidos y abucheo. Una cruda realidad a la que el exentrenador del Real Madrid no es ajeno: "Entiendo perfectamente su decepción y la compartimos. Lo único que podemos hacer es trabajar, intentar dar lo mejor de nosotros para revertir la situación y hacerlo mucho mejor". "Fue un partido duro, con un resultado difícil de asimilar. Tengo la sensación de que estamos en un momento delicado, cuando sufrimos un revés, no somos capaces de recuperarnos con la suficiente rapidez para alcanzar el nivel competitivo necesario contra un equipo como el Leeds". El bajón es innegable. El Chelsea sólo ha ganado uno de sus últimos cinco partidos. Cayó eliminado en Copa de la Liga, por penaltis, ante el Liverpool y en Premier ha caído hasta la octava posición. Después de once jornadas, figura a cinco puntos de la teórica 'zona Champions' y a 12 del Arsenal, líder en solitadio. Una inercia que Xabi Alonso espera cortar este mismo fin de semana en su visita al Nottingham Forest. "Hemos perdido parte de la confianza con la que estábamos jugando y tenemos que recuperarla juntos. Tenemos que ser más fuertes. Es algo obligatorio en esta competición", reconocía el técnico 'blue'. No sólo se rebeló la grada. Jason Cundy, exjugador de Chelsea y Tottenham, fue un paso más allá en 'Talk Sport': "Ha sido una actuación preocupante, muy preocupante. Si esto sigue así, Alonso no conservará su puesto, lo digo sin rodeos". "Es casi increíble lo mal que estuvimos, en serio, no estoy bromeando. Estoy preocupado... Me preocupa cómo va a ir esta temporada. Estoy siendo completamente honesto, no sé si vamos a terminar... parecemos carne de cañón", aseguraba Cundy. Toca mejorar. No queda otra.

articles.title: Warde Manuel Reportedly Will Remain Michigan AD Amid Search After Trev Alberts Hire Dropped
articles.summary: Warde Manuel's tenure as Michigan's athletic director will continue after the university called off Trev Alberts' planned hire.
articles.body:
Warde Manuel's tenure as Michigan's athletic director will continue after the university called off Trev Alberts' planned hire.

Per ESPN's Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel , Manuel has agreed to remain in the role until the school can find a replacement.

The move comes after Michigan announced Tuesday it would not move forward with Alberts' hiring.

"As a result of the information gathered as part of the employment process, the university has determined that the background check is not acceptable to the University," Michigan president Domenico Grasso wrote in a letter to Alberts informing him of the decision.

Alberts, who had been Texas A&M's athletic director since 2024, signed a memorandum of understanding last week to take the Michigan job on a five-year deal that would have paid him $3.2 million annually for the first two years with a 4 percent increase each year thereafter.

Alberts' attorneys say Michigan owes their client $17.2 million, while U-M was also set to pay a $4 million buyout to Texas A&M, per ESPN .

Manuel was set to step down as Michigan's AD on Dec. 31. The university announced in July it was buying out the remaining three years on his contract and he agreed to leave his post in the wake of a probe into the athletic department that came after an investigation into former Wolverines head football coach Sherrone Moore's relationship with his executive assistant.

As part of the separation agreement, Manuel was going to be paid a lump sum of $7.14 million and retain certain perks given to former athletic directors, including access to tickets for Michigan games.

The deal also prevented Manuel from taking a job as an athletic director or senior athletic adviser for another Big Ten school for two years.

Manuel, a Michigan graduate, was hired by his alma mater as athletic director in 2016.

Michigan's athletic program has won four national championships during Manuel's tenure, including the College Football Playoff in 2023, men's basketball tournament in 2026, women's gymnastics in 2021 and men's gymnastics in 2025.

articles.title: 'Pep'sadilla antes de Navidad en el City: "Estás pensando en 10 años con Guardiola, ahora todo ha cambiado"
articles.standfirst: El City suma 10 partidos recibiendo goles y encadena cuatro encuentros sin ganar en Premier
articles.summary: El City suma 10 partidos recibiendo goles y encadena cuatro encuentros sin ganar en Premier
articles.body: Enzo Maresca ha pasado de firmar el mejor inicio de un entrenador recién llegado a un equipo en la historia de la Premier -ganó los siete primeros partidos de Liga con el Manchester City- a verse envuelto en una 'Pep'sadilla antes de Navidad. Literal. Y es que el 'fantasma' de Guardiola -Maresca llegó a trabajar como asistente del español- sigue muy presente en el Etihad. Como si de la historia del señor Scrooge se tratara. "Estás pensando en 10 años con Pep [Guardiola] y ahora todo ha cambiado. Hay que pensar que llevamos cuatro meses juntos. Hay un entrenador diferente, jugadores diferentes... ¡Hemos cambiado el 50% de la plantilla! Estamos en plena transición, es normal que necesitemos tiempo", se defendía el ex de Sevilla y Málaga en 'Bein Sports' tras el 2-2 en Champions contra el Nápoles. El bajón que han experimentado los 'cityzens' coincidiendo con el anuncio de su condena resulta sintomático. Encadenan 10 encuentros recibiendo goles y cuatro partidos sin ganar en Premier. Tres derrotas contra Aston Villa (2-1), Brighton (0-1) y Nottingham Forest (3-1) y un empate frente al Fulham (1-1) que les sitúan terceros a seis puntos del Arsenal. El City volvió a gozar ante el 'Napoli' de un dominio abrumador, pero de nada le sirvió tener el 62,7% de la posesión ni realizar un total de 665 pases, casi la mitad (303) en el último tercio del campo. "Fue realmente sorprendente ver un City tan aburrido y predecible en la primera mitad. Si juegas contra un equipo que se toma su tiempo, te preparas. Es mucho más fácil defender. Te sientas y ves cómo el City pasa el balón una y otra vez, despacio, despacio. Puedes fumarte un cigarro", aseguraba Pat Nevin en la 'BBC'. Para prueba un ejemplo: Erling Haaland, que acumula dos partidos sin marcar, apenas tocó 14 balones. "Fue difícil atacar al Nápoles con un bloque bajo, once hombres muy abajo, defendiendo alrededor de su área", se justificaba Maresca. "Siento que estoy teniendo oportunidades más que suficientes para marcar", confesaba Haaland, visiblemente contrariado: "Siento una enorme responsabilidad. Lo único que quiero es rendir y ganar partidos con el Manchester City. Ahora mismo no lo estamos haciendo y eso duele". Haaland, sin embargo, no se escondió. Aprovechó para hacer autocrítica en 'Bein': "El fútbol es fácil y, a la vez, muy complicado. Sabes lo que hay que hacer, pero cuando pierdes te lo empiezas a cuestionar todo. Lo mejor sería no pensar, pero en este momento es muy complicado. No tengo idea de qué nos faltaba, pero en los últimos partidos se notaba que algo no funcionaba. Tenemos que averiguarlo y mantenernos positivos para sacar el máximo provecho de cada jugador". Que enfrente estuviera un mito 'cityzen' como Kevin de Bruyne tampoco ayudó. "Mientras tanto, con una extraña equipación naranja, el City apenas parecía el mismo. O al menos no el equipo que fue considerado el mejor de Europa en la época dorada de De Bruyne. El regreso de Kevin puso de manifiesto su declive", escribía Richard Rolly en 'The Independent'. "Estamos en una situación difícil", reconocía Rayan Cherki después de sumar una victoria -'in extremis' frente al RB Leipzig (2-3)- en los últimos siete partidos oficiales. "El City es vulnerable. En estos momentos son demasiado fáciles de superar y eso es un problema. No da la impresión de ser un equipo capaz de mantener su portería a cero y ése es probablemente, su mayor problema, y la estadística más preocupante de esta racha reciente”, se lamentaba Stuart Pearce, ex del Manchester City, en 'Talk Sport'. Un déficit que Maresca, lógicamente, ya había identificado. "Una vez más, con el balón, todos los números, todas las estadísticas, están a nuestro favor. Pero lo principal es el equilibrio entre lo que concedemos y lo que creamos...", deslizaba antes de ahondar en la 'herida': "En los primeros, más o menos, 10 partidos, no encajamos goles. Siempre marcábamos primero. Ahora es exactamente al contrario. Estamos encajando demasiados goles y necesitamos encontrar la manera de evitar eso". Para colmo, este fin de semana visitan al Arsenal. "Jugamos contra el campeón. Es el partido más difícil de la temporada, así que necesitamos una actuación 'top' de cada uno de nosotros", admitía Haaland. "No nos gustan este tipo de momentos en los que no ganamos... pero los jugadores tienen confianza. Tenemos que ser pacientes, trabajar, aprender y seguir adelante", insiste Maresca, que está viviendo su particular 'Pep'sadilla antes de Navidad.

articles.title: Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick for Liverpool vs Man Utd reveals 'grey area' as Mauricio Pochettino questions decision
articles.summary: Dominik Szoboszlai sparked Liverpool's rout of Man Utd with a free-kick goal after Leny Yoro was sent off, but should it have stood? United head coach Mauricio Pochettino believes Bradley Barcola was interfering with their defensive wall, although Bruno Fernandes appeared to push him
articles.body:
Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he received in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been overturned, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.

But Szoboszlai's goal from the free-kick Yoro conceded in the same incident was allowed to stand, with Pochettino believing it should have been disallowed because Liverpool winger Bradley Barcola was interfering with the Man Utd wall.

The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1m (1yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."

Pochettino referenced a similar decision last season when Eberechi Eze's goal from a free-kick for Crystal Palace at Chelsea was disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.

Pochettino said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall.

"Maybe in the last two years, they've changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].

"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed."

When Szoboszlai strikes the free-kick, Barcola is clearly within 1m of the United wall and, under the Laws of the Game, the goal should be ruled out.

However, a key difference between Eze's disallowed goal and Szoboszlai's free-kick is that Guehi shoves Caicedo and moves within 1m of the Chelsea wall, whereas Bruno Fernandes appears to push Barcola towards the Man Utd defenders.

In this case, it could be argued that Fernandes created the issue and Barcola ended up next to the Man Utd wall only because of his opponent's actions. The Laws of the Game do not provide an explanation for an attacker being pushed towards the defending team's wall.

VAR checks every goal and would have to decide whether it was a 'clear and obvious' error. Eze's goal was disallowed after the VAR had recommended a review to the referee over Guehi's involvement.

Another consideration is that Fernandes' push occurred before Szoboszlai struck the free-kick, meaning the ball was not in play, so it would not have been a foul by the United captain.

Had the referee spotted the push in the seconds before the free-kick was taken, he could have delayed the set-piece, disciplined Fernandes and then restarted from the original position.

Webb did not analyse the incident on the latest episode of Match Officials Mic'd Up.

Sky Sports News asked Pro Ref for comment.

articles.title: Leicester City: Owner Khun Top takes Foxes off the market
articles.summary: Leicester owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha confirms the one-time Premier League title winners are no longer up for sale.
articles.body:
Leicester City owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha has confirmed the one-time Premier League title winners are no longer up for sale and there will be a "refocus" on rebuilding the side after years of decline.

The Foxes were put on the market in the summer after back-to-back relegations saw the side drop from the Premier League and straight through the Championship to land in England's third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history.

A sales brochure was produced by US investment bank Citigroup in which an asking price of more than £200m was put on a League One club that a decade ago had defied all expectations by winning the Premier League title at 5,000-1 odds.

Leicester never publicly acknowledged that the club had been put up for sale, with under-fire chief football officer Jon Rudkin going so far as to say he "cannot comment on speculation" when asked about it in a rare interview with BBC Radio Leicester in October.

Khun Top, however, has now said that there were no takers when investment had been sought for a side that the Srivaddhanaprabha family, through its King Power duty free business in Thailand, have owned for 16 years.

"We recently undertook a structured process to explore whether new investment or a change of ownership could actually be the right thing for the club," Khun Top wrote in an open letter to Leicester City supporters on the club's website. , external

"Those discussions have not resulted in an agreement, and I have decided to conclude the process to enable us to refocus on the work needed to move the club forward."

'Business as always' - Foxes boss Martin brushes off sales talk

Listen to BBC Radio Leicester's When You're Smiling podcast

Pre-match, post-match and topical Foxes content

Three relegations in four years, having yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship before going down to League One, has badly damaged the relationship between the Foxes' owners and their supporter base.

While a golden age of success was bankrolled by King Power, with Premier League glory in 2016 followed up by FA Cup success in 2021, high spending on an underperforming side in recent years has led to an increasing number of supporters calling for Khun Top to sell up.

But the Thai businessman said he has a "deep connection" to Leicester and "its people".

And it is not just euphoric sporting moments that have forged the bond he is talking about, as his father - and predecessor as Foxes chairman - Khun Vichai died in a helicopter crash outside the stadium in 2018.

"For my family and me, Leicester City has been a big part of our lives for many years," he said.

"We have experienced extraordinary moments together, as well as some very difficult ones."

Khun Top added that the struggles of recent years, which included the club being hit with a points penalty last season for breaking spending rules, has got him "thinking a lot about our direction".

Earlier this year he told BBC Radio Leicester that he shoulders the blame for the club's decline.

"Making better decisions" as well as "continuing to learn from our past experiences" are two steps the club "need to take", he said.

Khun Top has insisted that through King Power, a company that has endured difficulties in recent years, the club's "financial position remains secure".

However, he added that there was "work needed to put Leicester City on a more sustainable footing".

"That has been a principle behind the work and decisions of the last year – giving the club the appropriate support for its immediate circumstances, while building the organisational discipline and financial resilience that will underpin a responsible plan for future growth," he said.

As part of Khun Top's missive, he confirmed that chief executive Kevin Davies will be stepping down from the role in December.

Davies had only been in the job since March, and was promoted to the position after a shake-up of a number of leadership roles.

articles.title: Leny Yoro red card rescinded but row goes on
articles.summary: Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool has prompted an unseemly difference of opinion between Man Utd and Pro Ref.
articles.body:
Leny Yoro's overturned red card against Liverpool appears to have turned into an unseemly difference of opinion between Manchester United and referees' body Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off after bringing down Liverpool striker Alexander Isak in the eighth minute of the 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Referee Sam Barrott sent off the France international, and the decision was backed up by video assistant referee (VAR) John Brooks.

It split opinion among pundits and fans. Would Isak have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens? Was it really a clear goalscoring chance?

First, a Football Association regulatory commission upheld United's appeal and cancelled the red card.

Then Pro Ref boss Howard Webb said the red card was not "clearly wrong" - just moments before United held a pre-match news conference.

Over to Red Devils head coach Mauricio Pochettino, who was fiercely critical of the decision, and in particular the VAR.

But how can Pro Ref still believe the decision was right when an FA commission said it was wrong?

BBC Sport looks at how the system works.

The stand-off between Man Utd and Pro Ref

So United won their appeal. Pro Ref would disagree. Could the two sides not just agree to differ?

"You ask me a question and I need to defend our situation and our club and our players," Pochettino said about Yoro's red card.

It continued a theme from his post-match news conference.

You can see why Pochettino would be keen to talk about the red card, rather than the performance of his players. After all, United had just lost the first game of his tenure. Was the Argentine keen to create a siege mentality?

You can also understand United's frustration - two of their biggest games of the season so far have been defined by refereeing decisions.

The first was the VAR error to allow Erling Haaland's match-winning goal in the Manchester derby, when Enzo Fernandez clearly committed an offside offence.

As for the Yoro incident, Pochettino reserved much his criticism for the VAR. United felt he only took a cursory look at where the ball would run.

It should be noted that Match Officials Mic'd up, on which Webb gave his views, was filmed on Monday evening - before the result of the appeal.

Would that change his opinion? Almost certainly not.

Webb acknowledged the argument against a red card, which was Isak would not get the ball. But he was adamant it was not such an egregious error that it required a VAR intervention.

So are we back to arguing about when VAR should get involved?

The VAR threshold is too high, until it is too low. Rinse and repeat.

It is the Premier League clubs, and not Pro Ref nor the FA, who set where the bar sits.

Take the last stakeholders' survey, which helps to shape how the game is officiated.

It found 65% wanted to maintain the current threshold for VAR intervention, 20% to increase it, and just 15% to lower it.

But, of course, where the Yoro incident sits is still a matter of opinion.

How confusing it must be for a supporter just watching on, hoping to understand.

An FA regulatory commission has said the red card decision was wrong. Case closed? Not so fast.

Pro Ref will not always agree with the decision of an appeal board, nor will they use it as a barometer for future decisions.

And the burden of proof for a VAR intervention is considered higher than for an FA commission.

Pro Ref places far more stock upon the judgements of the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

The KMI Panel creates the merit table for referees, and helps shape how decisions are made in the future - especially for the VARs.

But surely the FA is the higher body? Not quite.

The FA is responsible purely for disciplinary measures and has no say on how games at the professional level are refereed.

If the Premier League tells Pro Ref the decision is right or wrong, that counts far more than any vote by an FA commission.

BBC Sport understands the club argued that if Isak had maintained his top recorded speed, he would not have got to the ball first.

The club say that is objectively provable, within minutes, using data. This, they say, was not a subjective decision.

To argue it was not subjective goes completely against the nature of the decision - it required a referee's judgement.

Whatever this data was, it most definitely was not available to the referees. The VAR cannot call upon a 3D animation of each player, detailing their running speed and providing an objective result.

How much stock did the commission place on this evidence? We will not know until the written reasons are published in a few days' time.

But United are not going to let this lie, and Pro Ref is not going to bend.

Such is the way FA commissions work, you can never be sure who will win.

There are three panel members who are usually former players, but occasionally you might get a retired referee.

The role of the commission is not to "usurp the referee by re-refereeing the incident".

A designated referee delegate is present to answer questions on the laws of the game, but they cannot offer an opinion on the incident.

The only input Pro Ref has is the official's report - a short entry by the referee that says which law was used for the red card. There is no other context.

It will read something like this: "I have to report that I, as the referee, sent off Yoro, Leny of Manchester United FC Under Law 12 section: S5."

The burden is on the club to prove its case by submitting a body of evidence - videos, images and testimony.

There is no right of reply. The evidence is weighed up by the panel, a vote is cast and the majority wins.

It makes predicting the outcome notoriously difficult, as the system is an opinion poll based upon a club trying to persuade at least two people to agree with them.

Take a look at Aston Villa 's successful appeal against Douglas Luiz's red card for violent conduct four years ago. Luiz had been sent off via a VAR review for a headbutt on Aleksandar Mitrovic.

The panel's written reasons stated the appeal was won partly because Luiz was "a few inches shorter than Mr Mitrovic so his forehead is naturally at the same height as Mr Mitrovic's nose/face as the two players come together".

So, when the two players bumped chests the headbutt was just an accident. Appeal upheld because Luiz was a bit shorter.

Some might think anything is worth trying.

articles.title: Así se reparte el Cádiz en los despachos: Septien y Contreras suman la mayoría
articles.standfirst: El club ha mostrado una distribución accionarial con el presidente y el vicepresidente al frente y Quique Pina, Manuel Vizcaíno y Ben Harburg entre los propietarios
articles.summary: El club ha mostrado una distribución accionarial con el presidente y el vicepresidente al frente y Quique Pina, Manuel Vizcaíno y Ben Harburg entre los propietarios
articles.body: El pasado mes de julio, Manuel Vizcaíno dejó la presidencia del Cádiz CF después de doce años en el cargo y el empresario mexicano-alemán Christian Septien tomó el relevo. Desde entonces, las preguntas sobre el futuro del club también han mirado a los despachos. La ampliación de capital y la escisión de Sport City han puesto el foco en una cuestión: ¿quién tiene las acciones del Cádiz?S El club mostró una distribución durante la comparecencia de su vicepresidente, Rafael Contreras, de este martes en la que trató de explicar la ampliación de capital y la polémica relación del Cádiz con Nomadar, la empresa que cotiza en el Nasdaq y que ha sufrido un desplome importante desde su salida a la bolsa estadounidense en octubre de 2025. Según los datos proyectados por el propio club, el grupo de Septien cuenta con el 30,93 % del capital y el de Contreras, con el 26,77 %. Juntos reúnen el 57,70 % y forman el bloque mayoritario que respalda la gestión del consejo de administración. Por detrás de los grupos del presidente y el vicepresidente aparecen Calambur y Leader Sport, sociedades vinculadas a Quique Pina, con un 20,45 % del capital. También sigue teniendo un peso importante Manuel Vizcaíno. El expresidente figura con el 17,15 % de las acciones, mientras que el empresario estadounidense Ben Harburg aparece con un 4%. El 0,71 % restante corresponde al resto de accionistas. La fotografía accionarial llega en medio del debate sobre el futuro societario del Cádiz. El pasado viernes, la junta aprobó la escisión de Sport City Cádiz, una operación que plantea que las participaciones de esta sociedad dejen de pertenecer directamente al club y pasen a sus accionistas. La escisión forma parte de una reorganización más amplia que contempla que Nomadar, la empresa que cotiza en el Nasdaq, pueda llegar a convertirse en accionista mayoritaria del Cádiz mediante operaciones posteriores. Su ejecución, sin embargo, quedó frenada provisionalmente por una medida judicial comunicada por Calambur. Contreras defendió que “la escisión no representa la parte de control de Nomadar” y aseguró que el proyecto permitiría acceder a mercados internacionales para invertir en el club. Por otro lado, Ben Harburg también ha mostrado públicamente su rechazo a la operación y ha anunciado acciones legales. El Cádiz ha mostrado así una parte de su mapa de poder mientras la afición tiene muchas dudas y preocupación por el futuro del club y su vinculación Nomadar. Lo llamativo es que la propia empresa ha reconocido "dudas sustanciales sobre su capacidad para seguir operando" .
