articles.title: Jude Bellingham: Real Madrid midfielder said to be 'best in world' - but where does he rank?
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho called Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham "the best midfielder in the world", but where would you rank him?
articles.body:
Is there a better central midfielder on the planet than Jude Bellingham right now?

Not according to Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid manager might be trying to manage the Englishman's minutes, but he did not hold back in his praise after the 23-year-old came off the bench and scored a superb volley , helping Real overturn a half-time deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

"He has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything," Mourinho said.

"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world."

Bellingham's impressive 45-minute cameo came just nine days after an outstanding, all-action display for England in a 3-2 Nations League win in Spain.

While the former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund player also earned plenty of plaudits for his displays at the 2026 World Cup, where he scored seven times, Mourinho believes Bellingham's unique blend of craft and graft isn't yet fully appreciated.

"He can play as a '10', as an '8', with two pivots, with one," Mourinho said after the win against PSV. "That's why I said, when the Ballon d'Or was discussed, that it was outrageous he wasn't among the top 10."

While wingers like Lamine Yamal or Michael Olise are also likely to be contenders for the 2027 award, is there anyone you would rather have in central midfield than Bellingham?

BBC Sport looks at what makes him so good, and who his closest challengers are.

Although only 23, Bellingham is already in his fourth year at Real Madrid and is on course for his most productive campaign since his debut season in 2023-24, when he scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists, including setting up Vinicius Jr in the Champions League final.

He has seven goals and four assists in 18 appearances this season. Only three central midfielders have more goal involvements across Europe's top five leagues, but Bellingham's all-round game is what sets him apart.

He leads his Real team-mates for possession won, duels won and fouls won. And while only Kylian Mbappe has had more shots on target, Bellingham offers far more than just late runs into the box.

He has played more passes into the final third than any other Real player, leads the club for ball carries and is second only to Arda Guler for chances created.

When Bellingham's coaches at Birmingham gave him the number 22 shirt, it reflected their belief that he could play any role, as a number 10, 8 or 4.

He has fulfilled that potential to become the complete midfielder.

While Bellingham made his senior debut with Birmingham, Vitinha also spent part of his formative years in the Midlands, scoring once in 22 appearances during a loan spell at Wolves - a spectacular long-range strike against Chorley in 2021.

But goalscoring isn't what the Portuguese playmaker is best known for - it is his metronomic passing.

The 26-year-old has played a pivotal role in Paris St-Germain's back-to-back Champions League triumphs, with manager Luis Enrique saying he "embodies the perfect midfielder".

He was named man of the match in the victory over Arsenal last season, having completed 141 of his 150 passes, matching the Champions League final record set by Barcelona's Xavi in 2011.

Vitinha finished third in the Ballon d'Or voting in 2025 but slipped to 14th this year, a ranking Luis Enrique disagreed with.

"It's a real pleasure to have a player with such physical abilities and that mentality," the PSG boss said last month. "He's at an incredible level."

Rice finished one place below Vitinha, and four below England team-mate Bellingham, in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings after helping Arsenal win their first Premier League title since 2004.

He briefly played at centre-back as a youngster at West Ham before establishing himself as a top-class defensive midfielder for the Hammers. But since joining the Gunners in 2023 he has taken his game to another level, adding significantly more attacking output.

Rice created 17 big chances in the Premier League last season, as defined by Opta, a total bettered only by Bruno Fernandes and Rayan Cherki.

The 27-year-old has also registered 14 assists in all club competitions since August 2025. While set-pieces have undoubtedly contributed to that tally, he offers much more.

He ranks among the top 4% of central midfielders across Europe's top five leagues for progressive carries, while posting similarly impressive figures for chances created, touches and expected assists.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner missed Spain's Nations League defeat by England this month through injury, and his absence was keenly felt as the hosts uncharacteristically struggled for control, at least against 11 men.

It was a far cry from Spain's triumphant Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup campaigns, both of which ended with him being named player of the tournament.

The 30-year-old completed 756 passes as Spain won their second global title, the highest total ever recorded at a World Cup.

His performances this summer were all the more impressive given that he had taken time to return to his best after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament, an injury that sidelined him for most of the 2024-25 campaign.

The former Manchester City player has slotted in seamlessly since joining Barcelona in August, and averages 106 successful passes per 90 minutes in La Liga - the second-highest figure, behind Vitinha, of any player in the top five European leagues.

The student playing in La Liga: Introvert Rodri's unique rise to top

Pedri may be six years younger than Rodri, his midfield partner at the Camp Nou, but he boasts extraordinary experience for a 24-year-old, having made more than 250 appearances for Barcelona, not to mention playing at two European Championships and two World Cups.

The Tenerife-born midfielder combines tigerish work-rate with quality in possession.

He has created 26 chances from open play in La Liga this season, the sixth-highest total across Europe's top five leagues, and wins possession an average of 7.6 times per 90 minutes, the 10th-highest figure.

However, such is Spain's wealth of midfield options that he is not even guaranteed a starting place for his country, with Fabian Ruiz preferred for their final three matches at the 2026 World Cup.

Paris St-Germain midfielder Ruiz, who finished 10th in this year's Ballon d'Or rankings, also deserves to be in any debate about the world's best midfielders.

He might not yet have the profile of Barcelona team-mates Rodri or Pedri, but on current form alone, versatile youngster Lopez is one of Europe's best box-to-box goalscorers.

The 23-year-old already has nine goals and seven assists this season. Counting only goals scored in Europe's top five leagues and the Champions League, no central midfielder has more.

While Lopez can also operate on the wing, the presence of Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon means he has mainly featured as a number eight or a number 10 this term.

The Barcelona academy graduate played only a bit-part role as Spain won Euro 2024 and was unfortunate to miss the World Cup after breaking a bone in his foot in May.

However, a summer off enabled him to hit the ground running this season, and he has not looked back.

articles.title: Uno a uno del Barça vs Sabah: Lo de De Jong ya no es un experimento
articles.standfirst: Analizamos el rendimiento de los jugadores azulgranas y el planteamiento de Hansi Flick
articles.summary: Analizamos el rendimiento de los jugadores azulgranas y el planteamiento de Hansi Flick
articles.body: Hansi Flick revolucionó el once en el encuentro contra el Sabah. El técnico alemán, consciente de la gran carga de partidos que tiene el equipo, sorprendió con la presencia de Balde en el equipo. Fue la primera titularidad del catalán esta temporada que fue de menos a más pero, cuando más cómodo estaba, se lesionó. Gavi también saltó de inicio. Lo que ya no es una sorpresa es la presencia y el rendimiento de De Jong en la zaga. El neerlandés está muy cómodo jugando atrás. Ha pasado de ser un experimento a una solución más que solvente cuando el equipo tiene tantas lesiones. El internacional, tras la lesión, está a un gran nivel. Primera parte: Joan García no pudo mantener la meta a cero. El de Sallent tuvo dos intervenciones buenas en el primer tiempo. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Encajó una diana Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Koundé regresó al once tras haber estado un mes lesionado. El francés ya sumó unos minutos contra el Villarreal. Poco trabajo en defensa y poca incidencia en ataque, más allá de alguna jugada puntual. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Sin sorpresas Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: El neerlandés sigue en la defensa y formó junto a Gerard Martín. Fue el encargado de arrancar la jugada y solía buscar a Pedri. Pese a que no es central, De Jong está cómodo en esta demarcación. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Sin demasiado trabajo en el segundo tiempo. Nota al final: 7 Primera parte: Gerard Martín se mantiene en el once. Como siempre, correcto y atento. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Muy correcto Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Primera titularidad de Balde esta temporada. El lateral no entra en los planes de Hansi Flick este curso, pero en Bakú volvió a tener protagonismo. Sin duda, fue una de las sorpresas del once. Fue de menos a más en el primer tiempo e, incluso, se atrevió con un disparo desde la frontal. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: El canterano dio la asistencia del gol a Adeyemi. Cuando mejor estaba, tuvo la mala fortuna de lesionarse el tobillo. Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Pedri tampoco rotó, aunque fue sustituido en el descanso. El canario intentó generar juego, pero costaba encontrar líneas de pase. Fue el futbolista más activo en los primeros compases y cuando el bloque estaba más espeso. Incluso, el primer remate entre los tres palos del Barcelona llevó su nombre, en el minuto 20. Nota al final: 7 Primera parte: Tercera titularidad esta temporada de Gavi, que no está teniendo protagonismo. Se movió y se ofreció continuamente. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Dejó el campo a falta de cinco minutos para el final. Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Adeyemi fue el encargado de suplir al lesionado Lamine Yamal por la derecha. Sin suda, el Barcelona apostó por la velocidad, con Gordon y el alemán en los extremos. Fue la primera vez que encadenó dos titularidades. No terminaba de lograr ese último pase ni de encontrar los tres palos. Eso sí, un remate del alemán que rechazó el portero, permitió a Gordon lograr el primero. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Finalmente, el alemán encontró el camino del gol en el 55' a asistencia de Balde. Tuvo gasolina para completar los 90 minutos sin parar de correr. Nota al final: 6,5 Primera parte: Aunque el andaluz lleva muchos minutos en sus botas, no entró en las rotaciones. De todas formas, no podrá jugar los dos próximos compromisos por sanción. Muy discreto en los primeros minutos de partido. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: No estuvo fino en el gol del Bakú. En líneas generales, no fue un gran encuentro del andaluz. Nota al final: 6 Primera parte: Hansi Flick dosificó al inglés en el encuentro contra el Villarreal del domingo y en Bakú salió de inicio. En los primeros compases, entraba en contacto con el balón, pero con poco peligro. A la media hora, marcó el 0-1 en un balón que despejó mal el portero. Tres minutos después, le anularon un tanto por fuera de juego en el inicio de la jugada. Nota al descanso: 7 Segunda parte: Volvió a aprovechar un rechace del portero, tras disparo de Gabriel Jesus, para lograr el segundo de la tarde. Fue uno de los jugadores más incisivos de la tarde. Dejó el césped en la recta final. Nota al final: 8,5 Primera parte: Gabriel Jesus fue el jugador elegido por Flick para la punta de ataque. Descansó Raphinha. También discreto, y poco acertado cara a puerta, en el primer tiempo. Nota al descanso: 5 Segunda parte: Pese a que estaba firmando un partido muy discreto, logró poner el cuarto en el marcador tras aprovechar un rechace del portero. Nota al final: 6 Salió en el descanso y pudo sumar 45 minutos tras la lesión. Además, con la sanción de dos partidos a Fermín, será titular contra Dépor y Atlético. Buenos minutos del internacional. Nota al final: 6 Debutó en el minuto 64. Nota al final: 6 Saltó al campo en el 64' tras la lesión de Balde. Nota al final: 6 Entró en el 76'. Nota al final s.c. Primera parte: El preparador ha apostado por las rotaciones e, incluso, por una pequeña revolución. Se le vio muy serio durante gran parte de la primera mitad. Nota al descanso: 6 Segunda parte: Movió el banquillo ya en el descanso buscando aún repartir más minutos. Se enfadó con el gol encajado. Nota al final: 6 Pudo jugar los últimos cinco minutos en la medular, su posición natural. Nota al final: s.c.

articles.title: MLS Reportedly Finalizes 16-Team Playoff Bracket Format for 2027 Season
articles.summary: Major League Soccer is reportedly ready to introduce a 16-team playoff bracket format for the 2027-28 season.
articles.body:
Major League Soccer is reportedly ready to introduce a 16-team playoff bracket format for the 2027-28 season.

As reported by Paul Tenorio and Tom Bogert of The Athletic, the new system will include home-and-home series and single elimination-styled knockout matches.

It is suggested MLS owners preferred an easy-to-follow format over a more complex option, such as taking inspiration from Australian Rules Football with a style that would have expanded the playoffs to 20 teams.

The upcoming changes will instead see 16 teams qualify, two fewer teams than the current season, with extra time and penalties included as tiebreakers, rather than away goals or seeding.

These tweaks also align with MLS switching to a season that runs from July to May, bringing it closer in line to the European football calendar. It'll feature 27 matches, a middle ground to the current format that lands between 25 and 33 games.

Tenorio and Bogert's report adds that it's critical the league continues to create meaningful matches that produce significant fan interest and home gates, with many teams currently losing money.

Fewer spaces to qualify should add weight to the regular season, with teams less likely to coast while trying to secure a route to the playoffs Right now, a lack of jeopardy at both ends of each conference can play into MLS campaigns losing steam.

Vancouver Whitecaps star Thomas Muller, one of Europe's most decorated names, previously voiced concern over a lack of consequence due to there being no relegation in the American league.

"There is no relegation, there is no big pressure," Muller told Global News (h/t Ali Rampling of The Athletic) "There is: we do a rebuild. Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated."

Such a system certainly provides major drama, and often intensifies support, for sides battling to maintain their top flight status. In many cases, escaping the drop can be a triumph on par with winning a trophy.

The new playoff format system could be the route to similar nearer the top of the table, adding weight to matches that have a tendency to become stale in the league's current guise.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest: Oliver Glasner unhappy with Forest standards
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner has questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after being in the country for a number of years.
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner says standards at the club were not good enough when he arrived, and has questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after being in the country for a number of years.

Forest are one place above the relegation zone heading into Friday's home game against Chelsea , winning just two of their first 11 games in the Premier League.

"Stability in a company is having standards," said Glasner. "Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

"We have players who are here for four years, can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

"For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English. If I want to manage in Italy, I have to speak Italian.

"Otherwise, Oliver Glasner, if you want to speak in your dialect, stay at home in Austria, everybody understands you, but nowhere else."

Forest, who narrowly avoided relegation last season but who did reach the Europa League semi-finals, have had a succession of managers in recent years and while Glasner refused to blame the upheaval for any problems he has inherited, he feels standards need to rise.

"We want to create a stable Nottingham Forest team that can consistently play in the top half of the Premier League," added Glasner, 52.

"We are a few steps away from this but we really believe we know which steps we have to take.

"We are still very ambitious but it looks to take a little bit longer than we all hoped. The goal is getting stability into this club and we're still working on this.

"We knew this is a transition season, let's say like this, where we still stay very ambitious but with a lot of problems to solve."

Glasner held transfer talks with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis in London on Monday as the club prepares their plans for the January transfer window, when they hope to add up to five players to their squad.

"He [Marinakis] was asking 'what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment'," said Glasner.

"He wants the best for Nottingham Forest , he wants the best for everyone here.

"We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling."

articles.title: SEC denied temporary restraining order in federal lawsuit against LSU as it considers expelling school
articles.summary: The conference sought permission for emergency relief to potentially pave the way for the SEC to expel LSU, but a federal district court judge ruled against...
articles.body:
The SEC has been denied a temporary restraining order by a federal judge in its fight with LSU, according to AL.com's Matt Stahl .

The conference sought permission for emergency relief to potentially pave the way for the SEC to expel LSU, but U.S. District Judge Annemarie Axon ruled against the conference on Wednesday.

The SEC can still continue with its scheduled meeting on Thursday, Dec. 3, to consider the expulsion of LSU. But it does not currently have the protection of a federal court ruling now , which opens the door for legal challenges from the school.

The SEC and one of its most prominent and longstanding members have been at odds for months, but the latest row involves LSU men's basketball coach Will Wade electing to play in a game RJ Luis , who had previously signed a two-way deal with the Utah Jazz and saw NBA preseason action after going undrafted last year.

It's a similar legal fight the school had earlier this fall when a judge cleared a path for multiple players to join LSU's football roster despite having been rostered in NFL training camps earlier this summer. Those players never ended up making the Tigers' roster .

The latest federal lawsuit sought to prohibit LSU from "taking any action, including filing, prosecuting, or participating in lawsuits or otherwise seeking judicial intervention, to deter, coerce, prevent, or punish the Conference for exercising its First Amendment right of free association, including through potential termination of Louisiana State University."

Luis will sue the SEC and its commissioner, Greg Sankey, for violating the preliminary injunction that made him eligible at LSU, Luis' attorney, Tony Clayton, told ESPN on Monday night.

Luis, a former St. John's star, is seeking "a large number" in damages, Clayton reportedly said.

Clayton, per ESPN's report, is planning on deposing every SEC president. Searching for evidence that Sankey strung together a league-wide boycott of LSU after Wade played Luis last week, Clayton reportedly said he's already sent "preservation" letters.

articles.title: Bordalás: "Si queremos seguir vivos en Conference tenemos que ganar"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador azulón comparecía desde el estadio del Iberia de Tbilisi en la previa del duelo de Conference League
articles.summary: El entrenador azulón comparecía desde el estadio del Iberia de Tbilisi en la previa del duelo de Conference League
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa en la previa del duelo frente al Iberia 1999. Desde el estadio, en Tbilisi, el técnico azulón enmarcó la importancia del choque y señaló que, para que el equipo siga vivo en Conference, necesita el triunfo. Iberia: "En el fútbol actual las diferencias cada vez son menores, tenemos un gran respeto al Iberia, es el actual campeón, va a jugar con el apoyo de su afición y va a ser difícil. Estamos obligados, venimos con ganas de conseguir una victoria puesto que tenemos solo un punto. Nuestras opciones pasan por ganar mañana, como le ocurre al Iberia. Va a ser muy disputado, le tenemos un gran respeto. Venimos de una derrota dolorosa, no estamos bien en Liga. Si queremos seguir vivos en Conference tenemos que ganar". Recursos: "Está siendo una temporada difícil, lo sabíamos desde el inicio del campeonato. Se está comprobando, así lo pronosticamos. Sabemos que tenemos que seguir trabajando, seguir sufriendo y no queda otra que competir al máximo. El sentir de la gente es ese, estamos obligados a competir y hacer un buen partido". Carvajal: "Dani Carvajal es un chico que ha llegado fuera de mercado, estaba en el paro, es un jugador con mucha experiencia. Ojalá podamos clasificarnos y podamos contar con él. En Liga es un jugador que nos viene bien por su experiencia, no solo en el campo, también fuera. Esto es un equipo, todos los jugadores tienen talento, potencial. No estamos sacando el potencial que tenemos y, de alguna manera, estamos obligados a darle la vuelta a la situación". Dificultades: "No tenemos buenos resultados desde el comienzo, tenemos un déficit. Tenemos que mejorar tanto a nivel defensivo como a nivel ofensivo, nuestras prestaciones tienen que ser mucho mejores. Estamos en una liga muy competitiva e igualada. En Conference pasa un poco lo mismo, no hemos sacado buenos resultados, solo tenemos un punto y todo pasa por el partido de mañana. Respeto máximo al Iberia, pero si queremos seguir vivos o tener posibilidades de continuar, todo pasa por el partido de mañana. Venimos con ilusión y ganas de revertir la situación".

articles.title: Kirk Herbstreit Contract Agreement Rumors Denied by ESPN, Timeline for Deal Updated by Network
articles.summary: An ESPN spokesperson told Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports that the company and sportscaster Kirk Herbstreit are "not close to an agreement" as the contract for the College GameDay analyst and top college football color commentator for ESPN and ABC gets set to expire after the season.
articles.body:
An ESPN spokesperson told Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports that the company and sportscaster Kirk Herbstreit are "not close to an agreement" as the contract for the College GameDay analyst and top college football color commentator for ESPN and ABC gets set to expire after the season.

"We're not close to an agreement," the spokesperson told Glasspiegel. "We have communicated to Kirk's team that we are prepared to engage more directly after the college football season, and we're hopeful we can get something done at that time."

However, multiple sources told Glasspiegel that ESPN is in fact "closing in on a long-term deal" with Herbstreit, who has been on College GameDay since 1996.

Herbstreit has also been ABC and ESPN's top college football game analyst since 2006. In addition, he's been Amazon's NFL game analyst alongside play-by-play announcer Al Michaels since 2022.

Ultimately, it would be shocking if the 57-year-old Herbstreit wasn't on ESPN next year. The former Ohio State quarterback been a fixture on the network for three decades and seems primed to continue working long-term there.

Per The Athletic's Andrew Marchand , Herbstreit signed a contract extension with Amazon in September. However, there is a catch.

"But the terms give Amazon flexibility to move on if one of its top targets, like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, becomes available, according to sources briefed on the decision who were not authorized to speak publicly," Marchand wrote.

Marchand reported that Herbstreit is in the final season of his five-year deal. His next deal with Amazon is shorter than his current contract, but the exact length and money terms were not disclosed.

articles.title: Uno a uno del Atlético contra el Viking: los delanteros rompen su 'sequía'
articles.standfirst: Analizamos el rendimiento de los jugadores rojiblancos y el planteamiento de Simeone
articles.summary: Analizamos el rendimiento de los jugadores rojiblancos y el planteamiento de Simeone
articles.body: Simeone deja en el banquillo a dos indiscutibles como Barrios y Giuliano y vuelve a dar una oportunidad a Sorloth. El mejor portero de la historia del Atlético cumple hoy 111 partidos en Champions con la camiseta rojiblanca. PRIMERA PARTE: Muy atento para abortar una llegada del Viking saliendo a despejar fuera del área y muy seguro en general, transmitiendo su habitual seguridad. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 6 Tras ejercer de mediocentro frente al Bayern, regresa al lateral derecho. PRIMERA PARTE: Echó en falta las ayudas de Giuliano en las primeras acciones de ataque del Viking. Tuvo una pérdida peligrosa justo antes del descanso que a punto estuvo de meter a los noruegos en el partido. No fue su mejor primera parte. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 5 SEGUNDA PARTE: Arrancó con otra cara, ganando la línea de fondo nada más empezar para servir un balón a Sorloth que el 9 no llegó a empujar en boca de gol. Después de su aseado partido en Getafe, afronta su 'redención' en la Champions tras el error que allanó el camino al triunfo del Bayern. PRIMERA PARTE: Centrado, triunfador en sus dos primeras disputas importantes, eso le dio confianza incluso para cuando tuvo que jugar el balón. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 6 El futbolista de campo más utilizado sigue 'silenciosamente' como inamovible. PRIMERA PARTE: Dominante en el juego aéreo, sobresalió en los centros laterales. Vital también en el origen del 1-0, filtrando un pase a la subida de Grimaldo que sería medio gol. También se sumó al ataque más de una vez. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 9 SEGUNDA PARTE: Rozó el gol con un cabezazo tras adelantarse a la defensa rival que habría puesto la guinda a su completísimo partido. Su vocación ofensiva y su capacidad asociativa apuntan a ser claves para tumbar al Viking. PRIMERA PARTE: Una asistencia, tras un gran pase atrás, para sumar a su impacto en el ataque. Arregló el error de Llorente apareciendo como una centella en el área para evitar el remate del delantero del Viking. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 8 SEGUNDA PARTE: Es un defensa con alma de delantero, lo intentó con un intencionado disparo desde el borde del área que exigió otra gran parada. Pese a acabar cargado frente al Getafe, sigue en el once tras confirmarse en el 5 por excelencia del equipo. PRIMERA PARTE: A su función de ancla está sumando llegada al área: a punto de marcar a los dos minutos, pero su disparo fue repelido por un defensa. Volvió a finalizar un ataque a los pies del portero tras iniciar la acción en su campo con un autopase para enmarcar. Equilibrio y elegancia personificada. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 9 SEGUNDA PARTE: Siguió a un nivel espectacular: tan pronto volvió a asomarse a la frontal del área para controlar con el pecho y sacarse un disparo a la base del palo que paró milagrosamente el portero como se lanzó a los pies de un rival para repeler un misil dirigido a Oblak. Eterno. Ya son 121 presencias en Champions, 121 lecciones de fútbol. PRIMERA PARTE: Director de orquesta, también se asomó al balcón del área a disparar, pero la cabeza de un defensa desvió su trallazo. No se equivoca nunca, cuesta encontrarle un balón perdido. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 9 SEGUNDA PARTE: Acabó disfrutando de poco más de una hora con su hoja de servicios impoluta. Cuantos más años, más sabiduría. NOTA FINAL: 9 Aunque Simeone suele utilizarlo cerca del área, empezará en su puesto en la banda desde el que se forjó a nivel mundial. PRIMERA PARTE: En los dos primeros minutos ya dejó un taconazo y un pase atrás para que Cardoso gozara de la primera gran ocasión. Mereció el gol al filo de la media hora tras una parábola al palo largo, pero se topó con una gran mano cambiada del portero. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 7 SEGUNDA PARTE: Empezó de nuevo muy activo. Dejó una buena acción, regateando una y otra vez en busca de posición para el disparo antes de optar por filtrar un pase, en los diez minutos disputados antes de ser sustituido. NOTA FINAL: 7 La ocasión perfecta para trasladar su dulce momento a una Champions que le espera. PRIMERA PARTE: Trató de hacer gala de su condición de cañonero de LaLiga (nadie más ha marcado cuatro goles desde fuera del área), pero incompresiblemente el árbitro pasó por alto la mano con que un zaguero detuvo su tiro. Un gran socio siempre en el último tercio de campo. Sustituido al descanso en vista de la carga que lleva encima (con la selección lo juega todo) y lo que viene. NOTA FINAL: 7 Aunque se le viene resistiendo el gol en los últimos partidos, su juego va al alza. PRIMERA PARTE: Le estaba costando entrar en juego... hasta que se sacó de la manga un saque de falta marca de la casa a los 23 minutos: derechazo desde el vértice del área al ángulo del primer palo que el portero ya sólo pudo alcanzar cuando había sobrepasado la línea. El gol que tanto necesitaba. Muy asociativo, no se conformó, exigiendo al meta una buena parada tras otro disparo lejano. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 8 SEGUNDA PARTE: Siguió entendiéndose muy bien con Kang in y protagonizó una acción que levantó aplausos tras bajar al medio campo a robar un balón. Sin embargo, no le evitaría oír pitos también al ser sustituido. NOTA FINAL: 8 La motivación de jugar ante sus compatriotas debe ser el mayor acicate para que por fin inaugure su casillero goleador. PRIMERA PARTE: Lo que se le pide a un 9, primera ocasión, a la jaula tras un zurdazo inapelable. No apareció más rematar, pero dejó algún buen detalle como su gran pase para la oportunidad de Kang in. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 7 SEGUNDA PARTE: Aunque tuvo menos peso en el juego, lo peor fueron los gestos de molestias musculares con los que fue sustituido. NOTA FINAL: 7 SEGUNDA PARTE: Tras descansar de inicio, contó con la segunda parte para no perder ritmo. Nada más entrar ya hizo gala de su clase para servir a Llorente. SEGUNDA PARTE: Algo más de media hora para activarse. SEGUNDA PARTE: Ocupó el lugar de Julián. SEGUNDA PARTE: Relevó a Koke. SEGUNDA PARTE: Sustituyó a Sorloth, situándose en el flanco diestro. Aunque reserve a Barrios mirando a lo que viene, sale con un gran arsenal para ganar... y golear. PRIMERA PARTE: Fue a por el partido desde el inicio y en poco más de 20 minutos ya lo tenía resuelto. Con acierto en su apuesta por Sorloth incluido. NOTA AL DESCANSO: 8 SEGUNDA PARTE: Administró los esfuerzos de sus pilares con el cambio al descanso de Barrios por Baena, primero, y de Giuliano por Kang in y Julián, después.

articles.title: Anthony Gordon, 'non grato' en Azerbaiyán
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Sabah - Barcelona
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Sabah - Barcelona
articles.body: El Barcelona jugaba en Bakú con el reto de no distraerse y relajarse por su teórica superioridad contra un rival debutante este curso en la Champions League y también con el hándicap de jugar sin Lamine Yamal, baja por unas molestias en el tobillo derecho en esta quinta jornada de la fase de la liguilla del torneo europeo. Los de Flick cumplieron, de sobras, con las expectativas y ganaron el cruce por goleada gracias a su talento (sobre todo por el de Gordon) y, también, a causa de un Pokatilov generoso: no fue la mejor noche del meta de Kazajistán. El Barça tiene el objetivo de acabar entre los ocho primeros un poco más cerca. Hansi Flick revolucionó el once: hizo las rotaciones que anunció en la previa. Sorprendió, especialmente, la presencia de Alejandro Balde en el lateral zurdo: descansó Joao Cancelo de inicio. Fue la primera vez que el canterano culé salía de titular este curso. Había participado antes en cinco partidos, entre Champions (2) y LaLiga (3), y en ninguno había intervenido desde el principio. El joven zaguero intentó desdoblarse con Anthony Gordon y combinar con él sin dejar de cubrir a Severina. No desentonó. Estuvo activo, participativo y atento, dirigió conducciones meritorias e incluso se atrevió a chutar a puerta. Le dio la asistencia a Adeyemi. Se retiró lesionado: se hizo daño en el tobillo derecho. No está teniendo suerte. Frenkie de Jong volvió a jugar en el eje de la defensa. Suma seis encuentros este curso y en tres ha salido de central. Otro partido más en el que Flick sacrifica al neerlandés, que, dicho sea de paso, está dispuesto a sufrir y a jugar donde le manden si con ello beneficia al equipo a pesar de ponerse en riesgo. Acepta el reto, y su rendimiento está siendo para quitarse el sombrero. Tuvo un inicio titubeante en el Estado Olímpico de Bakú, pero pronto se entonó. Y fue decisivo. Interceptó balones y cortó acciones peligrosas, ofreció una acertada y limpia salida del balón, corrió sin mesura en todas las direcciones, lideró la zaga. Ha nacido un central. El extremo inglés volvió a marcar en el país caucásico. Firmó su primer doblete como azulgrana. Marcó cuatro de los seis goles que rubricó el Newcastle en febrero pasado, en la ida de la ronda intermedia de la Champions, al Qarabag (el resultado fue de 6-1), y anoche siguió con su racha. Jugó por la derecha, pero apareció por todos los lados del ataque: su velocidad le permite buscar siempre el mejor espacio y su inteligencia posicional, colocarse acertadamente para ofrecer el mejor disparo. Lideró, con autoridad y clase, la línea ofensiva. El centrocampista canario, que cumplía este 25 de noviembre 25 años, fue el mejor del partido. Impuso criterio en el juego, buscó líneas de pase, alargó al equipo, estuvo acertado en sus centros y pases, contuvo y le dio pausa al balón cuando fue necesario... y, además, provocó que Pokatilov se luciera con una gran parada a un derechazo suyo, de volea, en el balcón del área en el minuto 20. Flick hizo rotaciones y revolucionó el once, pero Pedri no descansó de inicio. Es un lujo que sabe que no se puede permitir... el partido en Azerbaiyán fue el enésimo ejemplo de que es un futbolista imprescindible. Tras el descanso, le dejó en el banquillo. El Barça ya dominaba en el marcador. El exprofesional del Borussia Dortmund sufrió para ganarle las espaldas a los defensas del Sabah, tuvo dificultades para entenderse con Fermín y para desdoblarse con Koundé, le costó conectar con sus compañeros y erró algunos pases que pusieron en peligro al equipo culé. Su primera parte no fue buena, aunque mejoró, algo, en la segunda. Se esforzó y se ofreció, y marcó. Pero no fue el mejor partido del internacional alemán. Las comparaciones son odiosas y seguramente tampoco son muy necesarias, estoy de acuerdo, pero está claro que la banda derecha es y debe ser de Lamine Yamal. O no, al menos, del germano, por lo visto en Bakú... El veterano meta del Sabah no tuvo su tarde y no guardará un grato recuerdo del cruce contra el Barcelona. Se lució ante un envenenado disparo de Pedri, y ya no hizo nada más. Fue su única acción meritoria, porque la parada a Cancelo en los minutos finales tampoco fue para enmarcar, aunque estuvo atento y atrapó el balón. Algo es algo. Pero quedó retratado en todos los goles del conjunto catalán y en casi todas las aproximaciones culés. Le costó blocar, se le vio inseguro y frágil en todos los acercamientos de los de Flick... El encuentro se le hizo eterno.

articles.title: Un paseíto por el fin del mundo
articles.standfirst: Cómodo triunfo de los azulgranas ante un flojo Sabah
articles.summary: Cómodo triunfo de los azulgranas ante un flojo Sabah
articles.body: El viaje a Bakú le salió redondo al Barcelona, que cumplió con todos los pronósticos pasando por encima del Sabah sin ninguna piedad. Consiguió los tres puntos sin ningún esfuerzo ante un flojo rival, que era el objetivo principal, pero también regresó sin ninguna tarjeta, otro detalle importante en esta competición. La alegría no pudo ser completa porque Balde tuvo que retirarse lesionado mediada la segunda parte. Flick ya había colgado el cartel de partido fácil a este choque. Solamente había que echar un vistazo al once que presentó. Muchas rotaciones pensando en lo que viene y en dar aire a sus jugadores más utilizados. El alemán sentó de entrada a Raphinha, Eric y Cancelo, además de Lamine que se quedó en Barcelona. Aprovechó la debilidad del Sabah para dar minutos a dos de los jugadores con los que menos ha contado esta temporada, como son Gavi y Balde, que entraron en el once. Los cambios se notaron en un equipo al que le costó coger el ritmo del partido. Los primeros minutos estuvieron llenos de confusión, con importantes errores en el pase de De Jong o Adeyemi. Pero el Sabah es limitado en ataque y eso se notó. Salió con velocidad en varias ocasiones, pero, a la hora de materializar las oportunidades, demostró por qué ocupa ese lugar en la clasificación. Tuvo una buena ocasión en un remate en semifallo de Lepinjica que acabó en el travesaño. Hubo otra oportunidad que detuvo Joan García cuando Aliyev se quedó prácticamente solo delante del portero. E incluso una más de Du Queiroz, cuyo remate se marchó alto. Con el paso de los minutos, el Barcelona fue adueñándose del partido. Le costó llegar a la portería de Pokatilov y todo el bagaje ofensivo se limitó a disparos desde lejos sin éxito. Pero, con el cansancio del rival, comenzó a crear peligro por las bandas, donde estuvieron muy acertados Gordon y Adeyemi. Entre ambos fabricaron el primer gol, cuando el británico aprovechó el rechace del portero después de un centro del alemán. El gol hizo daño al rival. A partir de ese momento, el Barcelona se hizo dueño del partido y, si no se fue con mayor ventaja al descanso, fue porque sus jugadores estuvieron muy fallones en el disparo. Los azulgranas remataron hasta 11 veces en la primera mitad, pero con un único tanto como bagaje. Pero los partidos hay que rematarlos. Y eso es lo que hizo rápidamente en la reanudación para evitar que la contienda se le complicase. Los tres delanteros cerraron el partido en apenas 15 minutos, en los que marcaron tres goles más para sentenciar el choque. Gordon, Adeyemi y Gabriel Jesús fueron los autores, aprovechando los regalos del equipo rival. Antes de acabar se produjo la mala noticia con la lesión de Balde. Mala suerte la del lateral, que acababa de dar la asistencia en el tercer gol a Adeyemi. Se marchó cojeando y con problemas hacia el banquillo. Con una enorme ventaja, el Barça se relajó y el Sabah lo aprovechó para reducir distancias después de un error de Fermín. El cabreo de Flick fue de órdago.

articles.title: MLS reportedly debuting new playoff format beginning with 2027-28 season
articles.summary: The new playoff format will go into place when the league switches to a summer-to-spring calendar beginning in July.
articles.body:
When Major League Soccer switches to a summer-to-spring calendar beginning in July, the playoff system will reportedly be getting a new look.

According to Paul Tenorio and Tom Bogert of The Athletic , MLS will unveil a 16-team, single-elimination format with home-and-home playoff series beginning with the 2027-28 season.

Currently, 18 teams make the MLS Cup Playoffs — nine from each conference. The No. 8 and No. 9 seeds in each conference play in a one-game wild-card match with winners advancing to a best-of-three first-round series. The remaining playoff rounds — conference semifinals, conference finals and MLS Cup final — are all winner-take-all one-game matches.

Under the new format, once the 16 playoff teams are decided, the matchups will feature two-legged series through the first two rounds that will be decided by extra time and penalties if the aggregate score remains tied after the second match. For the semifinals and MLS Cup, matches will be single elimination.

Beginning in 2027, the MLS regular season will run from mid-to-late July through April, with the postseason taking place in May. There will be a winter break beginning in mid-December through January with the second part of the regular-season schedule beginning in early February, likely after the Super Bowl. Another break will commence in June and July so as to not interfere with international competitions such as the World Cup, Euros, Gold Cup and Copa América, among others.

While not finalized, teams will reportedly play home and away against their division rivals and then once against the remaining MLS clubs for a 34-game schedule. Division winners would be guaranteed a playoff spot.

In preparation for the new season calendar, MLS will hold a 14-game "sprint" season from February to May 2027. The results will determine 2027 qualification for the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup, Canadian Championship, Leagues Cup and Concacaf Champions Cup.

articles.title: Hansi Flick: "Estoy contento por el triunfo, pero no por el gol concedido"
articles.standfirst: El técnico valora el cruce en Bakú de la quinta jornada de la Champions League
articles.summary: El técnico valora el cruce en Bakú de la quinta jornada de la Champions League
articles.body: Hansi Flick analizó este miércoles el encuentro de Champions League contra el Sabah disputado en Azerbaiyán. El Barcelona se impuso por goleada (4-1) en el cruce de la quinta jornada del torneo continental. Partido "Ellos han entrado con confianza, han provocado nuestros errores... lo más importante en estos partidos es marcar un gol. Estoy contento por los tres puntos, pero no por el gol concedido, porque es un error fácil. A este nivel, no puedes conceder ese tipo de acciones. Hemos cometido errores fáciles. Debemos mejorar. Pero son tres puntos importantes. En el inicio de la segunda mitad, hemos jugado con intensidad y hemos marcado tres goles". Goleadores "Son buenas noticias que marquen varios jugadores". Balde "Estaba haciendo un gran partido, pero se ha tenido que retirar. Le duele el tobillo. Hay que esperar a mañana jueves para saber qué tiene. Ha jugado muy bien, no es fácil para él no tener casi minutos y salir hoy, pero ha hecho un buen trabajo". Pedri "Está bien. El cambio ha sido para darle descanso. El plan era que jugara solo 45 minutos y, independientemente de lo que pasara en el partido, saldría después de ese tiempo y entraría Dani Olmo. A Olmo también estaba previsto que jugara 45 minutos, no más. Creo que eso fue positivo y estuvo bien, al igual que para los demás jugadores, en cuanto a la gestión de la carga de trabajo y el tiempo de juego. Estoy contento con el rendimiento de todos y de haber ganado por cuatro a uno". Jugadores suplentes "Estoy contento con su rendimiento, no suele ser fácil jugar en este tipo de partidos. El Sabah no tenía nada que perder, sólo tenía que ganar. Han hecho un buen trabajo y estoy contento con su esfuerzo y entrega. Son tres puntos más, importantes". Gabriel Jesus "No es fácil estar detrás de Raphinha, que siempre quiere jugar y es un hombre importante para nosotros. Gabriel tiene mucha calidad y es una persona positiva, se esfuerza... hablo con él. Ha ido marcando goles, es fantástico. Es importante disponer de jugadores como él, nos quedan siete partidos". Viaje "Sólo he visto el hotel y poco más. La gente ha sido muy amable. Es la tercera vez que vengo a Bakú. Se ha mejorado y hay una evolución aquí, en la ciudad y en el país. El Sabah juega la Champions... hace un buen trabajo. Y juega bien. Estoy feliz de haber ganado tres puntos y le deseo lo mejor a toda la gente del Sabah. Es importante seguir mejorando. Se ha hecho un buen trabajo".

articles.title: Trev Alberts drafting lawsuit against Michigan after school pulled his offer to be its next athletic director
articles.summary: Trev Alberts is seeking millions in damages from Michigan.
articles.body:
Attorneys for Trev Alberts are drafting a lawsuit against the University of Michigan and possibly incoming president C. Cybele Raver after the school pulled Alberts' offer to become its next athletic director, according to Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports.

The news comes after Michigan attempted to fast-track Alberts' hire with the school's current athletic director — Warde Manuel — retiring at the end of the year. But Michigan reneged on Alberts' offer after questionable quotes he submitted during a deposition in 2025 came to light. Manuel has since stated he'll remain with Michigan in 2027 if necessary .

During a deposition looking into a relationship between former Nebraska women's basketball player Ashley Scoggin and former assistant coach Chuck Love, in which Scoggin claimed she was groomed by Love, Alberts did not unequivocally say it was problematic for a coach and player to have a relationship, per USA Today.

Over a pair of depositions that lasted about seven hours combined, Alberts was asked by one of Scoggin's attorneys, Maren Chaloupka, if he believed college coaches should never have sex with athletes, especially since the university had a policy forbidding relationships between faculty and students, a rule that included coaches. Alberts responded that he "didn't know the answer to that" and then said "it depends" and there was "nuance" since eligibility rules following the COVID-19 pandemic meant some students were "25, 26 years old," and some of the coaches could be "27, 28."

Alberts was the athletic director at Nebraska at the time of the alleged relationship. He has issued a response to those quotes coming to light, calling them an "egregious characterization of words taken out of context."

Once those quotes emerged, Raver decided to pull Alberts' offer . That decision was made after Alberts already signed a memorandum of understanding with the school and before Raver's start date with the university. Raver's first day is expected to be Dec. 1.

After signing that memorandum of understanding (MOU) and agreeing to take Michigan's offer, Alberts reportedly started working "in various capacities" for the university, per Dellenger, a key point in his lawsuit.

That memorandum of understanding, which was acquired by ESPN, states that it serves as a "binding contract," potentially strengthening Alberts' argument.

After signing that MOU, Alberts resigned from Texas A&M, where he served as its athletic director. Additionally, since Alberts signed the document, he'll also be owed his buyout, which is reportedly more than $17 million .

The entire debacle has already painted Michigan in an embarrassing light. The school will now — presumably — be forced to shell out millions over pulling Alberts' offer. In addition to that, it may owe millions more if Alberts files and wins a possible lawsuit against the university.

articles.title: UEFA arregla el reloj pero la lía en la megafonía y deja a Julián Alvarez sin celebración en su gol de falta
articles.standfirst: Un error en la comunicación del autor del tanto provocó que en el estadio se cantase "Baena"
articles.summary: Un error en la comunicación del autor del tanto provocó que en el estadio se cantase "Baena"
articles.body: Lo que UEFA te da, UEFA te quita. Julián Alvarez tiene un gol más en Champions gracias a que el reloj de la tecnología de gol funcionó correctamente, pero se quedó sin celebración con la afición coreando su nombre por un fallo humano. Recapitulamos. En la jornada del martes, un error en la comunicación del reloj que debe avisar al árbitro cuando un balón traspasa la línea de gol provocó un incidente en el Feyenoord-Oporto. La muñeca del colegiado vibró pese a que la pelota no hizo ni el amago de entrar por completo en la portería portuguesa y el VAR tuvo que intervenir para corregir a la tecnología... que sí funcionó en el Metropolitano. El balón de la falta lanzada por Julián Alvarez entró por completo en la portería del Viking, el reloj avisó al colegiado Lambrechts y el gol de Álex Baena subió al marcador. ¿De Álex Baena? Según cantó la megafonía, sí. Un error de UEFA en la comunicación de la autoría del tanto provocó que la megafonía del estadio adjudicase el gol a Baena y no a Julián, que se perdió al Metropolitano coreando su nombre. Eso sí, al descanso, cuando los jugadores enfilaban el túnel de vestuarios, hubo rectificación y el argentino pudo escuchar su nombre por los altavoces del estadio.

articles.title: How Wake Forest became college football's biggest surprise — and why this magical run might be just the beginning
articles.summary: The Demon Deacons are crashing college football's party in a way nobody saw coming. And the unlikely architect of Wake's football revolution may have just pu...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — A few days after Wake Forest returned from a road trip to California and settled into its mid-October bye week, athletic director John Currie and football coach Jake Dickert found a nice bench on campus to sit down and have a hot dog.

"We just kind of talked about things," Currie told Yahoo Sports. "He didn't want to distract from the team, but what we knew was going to happen was there was going to be stuff coming at us, coming at our players, our assistant coaches. And the only way for us to control the controllable and reduce that distraction was to go ahead and get a deal done."

The "stuff," of course, was about other jobs.

When you've come out of nowhere to get Wake Forest into playoff contention — and the No. 8 Demon Deacons are arguably the hottest team in college football at 10-1 with a spot secured in the ACC championship game — speculation about where the coach is headed next is inevitable.

Currie, a veteran of three power conference AD jobs, knew exactly what was coming. By late September, he had already started to engage school president Peter Rodriguez, the board of trustees and key donors about putting together an extension and securing the resources it would take to make Dickert spurn interest from other schools.

Though Wake Forest partisans will point out that it has only employed three football coaches since the turn of the century — Jim Grobe stayed for a largely successful 13 years and Dave Clawson had a strong run for most of his 11 seasons — this season represents a different level of winning at a place most people wouldn't expect to be playoff-level good.

So Currie looked at a job market without a lot of successful, proven head coaches and a narrative that was going to be set by people who "don't understand why someone wants to stay at Wake Forest," he said. The only way to head off the approaching storm was getting a deal done.

Currie was prepared. Dickert, having moved around eight times in the last 15 years, was ready to settle and enjoy the fruits of his labor. And so earlier this month, they came to an agreement on an extension, clearing the path for Wake Forest to savor a season that, if anything, might be going a little too well. At this point, the only reason to doubt whether the Demon Deacons can do damage in the CFP is how easily they've handled everyone since late September.

Wake Forest has blown out so many teams the past couple months, the question of how they'll respond to adversity simply hasn't come up.

"If I didn't have the type of leadership we have on this team, I probably would [worry about that]," Dickert said. "The intensity with which we have taken the field and prepared has been really strong. As a coach, you always worry about different things, but at the end of the day, our team's playing at a really elite level."

How did Jake Dickert land at Wake Forest?

Dickert is musing about such a first-world problem after yet another rout, this time 50-29 over Georgia Tech in Atlanta. It was Wake Forest's sixth true road win of the year (all against power conference opponents) and its seventh straight game that was over before the fourth quarter.

Early in the season, before we really knew what Wake Forest was going to become, this was a team that needed overtime to squeak by Purdue and was in a long battle with Louisville before finally prevailing, 30-27. Since then, Wake Forest has operated with machine-like efficiency, winning its last six games ACC games by an average of 36.5 points.

You can certainly question the competition, but the level of dominance has been unambiguous.

"We knew we had a special group all the way back in January," senior defensive end Langston Hardy said. "We knew we had a deep team and throughout spring ball, we could really see how explosive this offense was. We just always kind of had that taste in our mouth that this is what we wanted to achieve and that's just the mission to keep going."

But how did this happen in the first place?

It all comes back to Dickert, a 43-year-old from Wisconsin who played D-III ball and then started his way up the coaching ladder at off-brand programs in the Midwest: North Dakota State, Minnesota State, South Dakota and South Dakota State just to name a few. At a couple stops along the way, Dickert was on the same staff as Jason Eck, whose work at New Mexico has made him one of the hottest names in coaching.

Dickert's big break came after the 2019 season when he was the defensive coordinator at Wyoming, which had gone 8-5. That led to Nick Rolovich hiring him as Washington State's defensive coordinator, and a year later, Dickert was unexpectedly thrust into the interim head coaching role when Rolovich and four other assistants were fired for refusing to comply with a mandate for state employees to take the COVID vaccine.

After a blowout win over Washington, Dickert was named the Cougars' permanent coach and did enough over the next three seasons to become a candidate for power conference jobs. In particular, administrators were impressed with his work in 2024 to get Washington State to 8-4 despite no conference affiliation, having been left behind by the 10 schools in the old Pac-12 that had scattered to other leagues.

In 2024, Clawson had given Currie a heads up that he might be ready to step away from coaching, but it was an awkward spot for an athletic director to start talking with candidates for a job that might not be open.

As Currie started looking at the landscape, he did not know Dickert personally but knew vaguely what qualities he was looking for. He leaned heavily on former Washington State athletic director Pat Chun (now at Washington) and Ben Sutton, a Wake graduate and former president of IMG College, to figure out how many of those boxes Dickert would check.

When Clawson officially pulled the trigger after the season, Currie was ready to act on a coach from the other side of the country that had the right attributes, even if his résumé was unconventional.

"No. 1, they've got to be smart," Currie said. "Our athletes are really smart, and if you're not smart, they'll see right through you. No. 2, they have to have character and integrity. And No. 3, they have to have been through something hard. You've got to have some scar tissue to do this job. And No. 4, you have to have accomplished something, and they had. And then you've got to have great energy."

At this point, it's worth noting that Currie might be known best across college football for controversy over his hiring acumen. At Tennessee in 2017, Currie fired Butch Jones and was set to hire Greg Schiano, who was Ohio State's defensive coordinator at the time.

Once the impending hire became public, the backlash from Tennessee fans became so intense that the school backed out of the deal by day's end. Currie, suddenly in scramble mode, criss-crossed the country to talk with others including Mike Leach, but the damage was done. Currie was fired five days later.

Though it was a gutting professional setback — Currie was essentially on the sidelines for a year and a half before getting the Wake Forest job — history has a way of correcting the narrative. Tennessee has certainly righted the ship now, but its decision to dump Currie was disastrous in the short term, as former football coach Philip Fulmer finagled his way into the AD chair and hired Jeremy Pruitt, who was neither good on the field or off it, getting the program into significant trouble with the NCAA.

Though Schiano might have crashed and burned, too — we'll never really know — the irony of it all is that Currie's hiring track record points to a pretty strong eye for what a program needs. At Kansas State, he brought in Bruce Weber, who led the Wildcats men's basketball team to the NCAA tournament in five of his first seven years, including an Elite Eight appearance. Though he was at Tennessee for less than a year, Currie identified Tony Vitello for baseball, a decision that eventually led to a national championship. And at Wake Forest, the Dickert hire and subsequent extension has changed the perception of what they're capable of.

A lot of athletic directors get caught up in geographic ties to the region (which Dickert did not have) or how familiar fans will be with a hire. Currie instead looked at the job Dickert did at Washington State and tried to figure out what skill sets would be translatable — like how he won eight games the year after quarterback Cam Ward transferred to Miami.

In the current environment of college football, it was a notable achievement.

"Similar to Wake Forest, they had to be disciplined in their approach," Currie said. "They're not picking off the top of the menu every year in recruiting, so they're identifying players they can develop."

And even though Wake Forest has never been considered a powerhouse football program, those kinds of players are everywhere in North Carolina, which has one of the fastest-growing populations in the U.S.

It has all added up to a narrative-busting conclusion: In the upcoming 24-team playoff era, there is a pathway for a program in Wake's category to regularly get a look at the postseason. As Currie points out, Wake would have been in a 24-team playoff in 2021 at 10-3 and would have been close in 2022 when they reached No. 10 before a late-season slide.

In other words, this isn't an Indiana-type story. This has been a solid program for a while, elevated by a combination of an elite head coach and institutional belief that it could break through. And all without the type of crazed, win-every-game-or-get-fired pressure that consumes so many power conference jobs.

When you consider all that, maybe it's not so surprising that Currie and Dickert came to an agreement pretty quickly to get a deal done and eliminate all the noise while they're bearing down on a CFP bid this year.

"I think for our people and our fans to have this moment in time, it shows once again that we can play in this mix," Currie said. "This makes it more real. We can be in it. It's going to be hard to be in this mix, but we can be in it. This will be the third time we've played in the ACC championship game. North Carolina and Duke played in it twice. NC State was never in it. So we're the best program in North Carolina and that's a huge advantage for us."

Now, with all the backstory out of the way, we get to another interesting question: How good is Wake Forest really? Good enough to win a first-round game? Put a scare into a team like Texas or Notre Dame in a quarterfinal? Get to a national championship game?

Some analytical models like ESPN's SP+ have Wake at No. 6, ahead of unbeaten Utah and Tennessee. Until this week, the committee was tepid because Wake Forest had not logged a win over a top-25 team. From a playoff perspective, the only great measuring stick we have was a 33-20 loss to Miami early in the season. Wake Forest fell behind 31-7 in that one but had the ball down just 13 points inside Miami's 15-yard line with plenty of time left.

Had Wake Forest scored there instead of an incompletion on fourth down, that game might have turned out differently.

Instead, a lot of eyeballs will be on Charlotte in a couple Saturdays when Wake gets its second shot at Miami in the ACC title game. Despite the tough news this week that running back Ty Clark is out of the season with an an upper body injury , all the evidence suggests the Demon Deacons are a much different team now.

"Our guys are well aware of where we're at, what we need to do, and the best part is we control our own destiny," Dickert said. "I don't really care about [doubters] if I'm being honest. Like, are they watching us? Are they really studying our players? Do they understand what [quarterback] Gio Lopez is doing? We have NFL players at every level on defense. Carlos Hernandez is one of the top three receivers in the country. Our offensive line peaking at the right time. Those are the facts when you watch the tape. Those are the only things we can control."

When you watch Wake Forest, there is an undeniable effortlessness in the way they're making this happen. It looks devastatingly physical up front, quick on the perimeter on both sides of the ball and very much under control offensively with Lopez completely rewriting his reputation after a lost 2025 season at North Carolina.

Everything about Wake Forest's play looks buttoned up and sustainable, but how do you put all these lopsided scores into context when they're beating teams that simply aren't capable of pushing back?

"If you're a Demon Deacon fan long enough, you know how hard this is," Dickert said. "What our team is doing is hard. I don't want people to miss that because I know sometimes we're making things look easy but this isn't easy. All the credit to the players. Our coaching staff is elite, and we've got the right magic right now as a team. But we need to continue to play a certain way."

Thanks to that conversation over a hot dog last month, Wake will have an opportunity to do it without distraction the rest of this season and perhaps well into the future.

"Our people are smart investors," Currie said. "So they see something that has validated the investment and trust that they have and then they see that we're not done. It's really hard to be in this position, but it's also not something that should just happen once and never happens again."

articles.title: Predicting Big Ten football scores in Week 13: UCLA vs. USC has plenty of CFP implications
articles.summary: The Big Ten likely won't have too many bids in the playoff, and there are some key games that will determine that.
articles.body:
It's the final weekend of the regular season of college football , and it's a big one. It's rivalry week and the Big Ten will have some classic showdowns in Week 13.

Michigan will travel to Ohio State for 'The Game', but that won't be the big matchup this season that fans are used to seeing. Neither team is vying for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, or a spot in the College Football Playoff.

But there are some impactful games this weekend. On Friday, Nebraska travels to Iowa, and on Saturday, USC and UCLA will square off, along with Washington and Oregon.

No Big Ten game has more College Football Playoff implications than USC-UCLA. The Trojans still have a long shot to make the playoff, but it's possible, and a win over UCLA would help Lincoln Riley's case. Also, a win over UCLA could end the Bruins' shot at making the playoff after starting the season 10-0.

Ty Dieffenbach suffered what appeared to be a serious injury in the loss against Michigan last weekend, but it sounds like it won't be a long-term injury. Still, Madden Iamaleava didn't appear ready for the spotlight when he came into the game against the Wolverines.

If UCLA is forced to play Iamaleava, UCLA's defense would need to play lights out to beat the Trojans. Not many teams can lose their starter and backup quarterback and remain competitive.

articles.title: USWNT embarks on Women's World Cup qualification at the CONCACAF W Championship
articles.summary: The pursuit of a fifth Women's World Cup title begins in earnest for the U.The United States will play El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Cha...
articles.body:
The pursuit of a fifth Women's World Cup title begins in earnest for the U.S. national team on Friday.

The United States will play El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the CONCACAF W Championship, which serves as the confederation's qualifying tournament for next year's World Cup in Brazil.

Win, and the United States is World Cup-bound. And while the world's No. 2-ranked team shouldn't have trouble against No. 78 El Salvador, nothing is guaranteed.

"I'll be leaning on our experienced players. They know how to do this, and they've been with us the longest to be able to deliver that," U.S. coach Emma Hayes said. "And I think the less experienced players have had a good body of work in the last couple of years. So we know what we need to do. We need to just make sure we come into camp with really clear minds about those things. Focus on the only game in front of us."

The United States has won four World Cups, most recently in 2019. The team had a disappointing finish in the 2023 tournament when they were eliminated in the round of 16 by Sweden. El Salvador has never played in a World Cup.

The United States, the defending W Championship winner, most recently played a pair of matches on home soil against defending World Cup champion Spain, losing the first 2-0 before playing to a 2-2 draw in the second.

But the U.S. squad will be without one of its biggest stars for qualifying. Trinity Rodman was injured in last weekend's National Women's Soccer League championship game. While the team characterized it as a minor shoulder injury, Rodman was replaced on the 23-player roster for the tournament by Jaedyn Shaw.

After El Salvador lost back-to-back matches to Paraguay in the October window, coach Eric Acuna sparked controversy when he publicly disparaged his team and called out individual players.

His comments were condemned by the nation's soccer federation, which said any statement that "discredits, belittles or publicly exposes in a derogatory manner" is unacceptable.

"Wearing the El Salvador jersey deserves respect, both in victory and in difficult times," the federation's statement said.

All four of the winners from the quarterfinals of the tournament this weekend will earn direct spots in the Women's World Cup.

Jamaica plays Costa Rica in the opening match Friday in Mansfield, Texas, following by the United States' game against El Salvador. Then on Saturday, Canada plays Panama and Mexico meets Haiti.

In addition to a spot in the World Cup, Canada is vying for 2028 Olympic berth. The top three finishers in the W Championship qualify for the Los Angeles Games. Should the United States be among the top finishers, the berth will include the fourth-place team because the U.S. has qualified as host.

Canada's best finish in the World Cup was fourth place in 2003. The team made it to the quarterfinals of the 2015 edition, which Canada hosted.

Ranked No. 9 by FIFA, Canada's squad features Chelsea defender Kadeisha Buchanan and Arsenal striker Olivia Smith. Also included were five players from the domestic Northern Super League.

Panama, ranked No. 45, hopes for a second World Cup appearance. In 2023, the squad was eliminated in the group stage.

The team's top scorer with 23 goals is captain Marta Cox, who plays professionally in Turkey.

Bunny Shaw leads the way for the Reggae Girlz

The Jamaican squad is ranked No. 40 but features one of the world's most dynamic players in Khadija "Bunny" Shaw, who plays for Manchester City and was one of the three finalists for the Ballon d'Or. Shaw leads the national team with 49 goals in 67 appearances.

The Reggae Girlz have earned berths in the past two World Cups and advanced to the round of 16 in 2023.

Costa Rica, ranked No. 41, made the World Cup field in 2015 and 2023, but were eliminated in the group stage both times. The team was a surprise runner-up in the 2014 CONCACAF W Championship.

Jamaica and Costa Rica will be guaranteed spots as hosts for the 2031 World Cup, along with the United States and Mexico.

Mexico, ranked No. 28 in the world, missed out on the last two World Cups. But the team has been on the rise, in part because of the growth of a domestic professional league, Liga MX Femenil.

Veteran Charlyn Corral, who plays in the domestic league for Pachuca, was recently awarded the Gerd Müller Trophy for best forward and goalscorer at the Ballon d'Or ceremonies. Corral has scored 53 goals in 89 games for Mexico since 2008.

Haiti, ranked No. 48, is led by former U.S. coach Pia Sundhage, who took over in February. The team's first World Cup appearance came in 2023, after upsetting Mexico in the group stage of the 2022 W Championship and then winning a spot via the intercontinental playoff, where they beat Senegal and Chile.

articles.title: Washington vs Oregon Prediction: Can the Ducks Close the Deal?
articles.summary: Oregon is the hot Big Ten team going, but can it get by Washington and roll into the Big Ten Championship? Here's the CFN game preview and prediction.
articles.body:
Oregon is the hot thing going for a Big Ten that's about as popular as that goopy green bean casserole hitting the table on Thursday. The Ducks found their groove after getting down early against Ohio State, winning four straight, with the last three each by double-digits. Now they have a chance to play for the Big Ten Championship with a win. Win two more in a row, go to the College Football Playoff. Washington can screw that up, though. The Huskies picked a terrific time to play their best ball of the year, including wins at Purdue, Nebraska, and Michigan State before all but ruining Indiana's season last week in a 27-24 overtime thriller.

Washington has won two straight and four of its last five games.

Oregon is trying to close out its fourth straight regular season with at least a five-game winning streak.

Oregon has won both games against Washington since the two programs joined the Big Ten. Washington's two wins over Oregon in 2023 won it the Pac-12 Championship on the way to playing for the national title.

Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections

The Huskies have been solid all year against the run, and there have only been a few meltdowns, but even when there's a little bending, there's not a lot of breaking. But the story has been the Dawgs trying to run the ball a bit more, and it meant everything against Indiana. This is hardly Army when it comes to the ground game, but quarterback Demond Williams Jr. took over against the Hoosiers, the offense made a point to grind it out a bit, and it set the tone early on against one of the nation's best run defenses. Yes, Oregon is playing well lately, but Michigan ran for 215 yards against the Duck D, Ohio State gave up on the ground and started winging it, and Michigan State was too battered to do anything right. Stay physical, and the Huskies can take control right away.

Oregon is finally playing like a team that knows it's really good. The talent was there from the start of the season, but the Ducks were stunningly sleepy. Quarterback Dylan Raiola has settled in, and now he's playing with confidence. The throws are more decisive, the running game is sharper, and the turnovers that were a disaster in the loss to UCLA, and an issue in the middle of the season have slowed. The Ducks haven't turned it over in any of the last three games, and penalties aren't an issue. Basically, the team is playing better and sharper, and Washington usually needs takeaways. It didn't come up with any in the win over Indiana, but before that, the team was 5-0 when forcing multiple takeaways, and 1-4 when it didn't.

Washington vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines

Can Oregon avoid being overconfident? Everyone is putting it in the College Football Playoff, which not only assumes a win in the Big Ten Championship, but also a win over Washington to get there first. Can the Huskies be salty like they were against Indiana? Yes, and they're going to make it a much nastier fight than the coronation the Ducks might like. It'll be close throughout, but the Oregon pass rush will start taking over late in a terrific primetime battle (even if it's at the same time as Auburn vs Alabama).
